1311.m: Spring and summer are breeding time.

1312.q: Where does the expression ‘goose bumps’ probably come from?
a: From the skin of a plucked goose with its little bumps
From the colour of the goose
1312.e: When a goose is plucked, its skin with the little bumps where the feathers grew looks like our skin when we are cold. That is where the expression comes from.
1312.m: Goose bumps come from plucked geese.

1313.q: How does a least weasel typically behave when there is danger?
a: It escapes into a hiding place in a flash
It attacks every enemy straight away
It always jumps into the water
1313.e: Thanks to its speed and agility, the least weasel can often escape into holes in walls or tunnels in time. This is its most important way of surviving.
1313.m: Running away is the best defence.

1314.q: What usually happens if a young swift falls out of the nest too early?
a: It often cannot get back and is in danger
It simply climbs back up the wall
The parents carry it back to the nest
It finds a new, better nest straight away
1314.e: Because of its short legs, a young bird that has fallen too early can hardly climb back by itself. That is why people sometimes take such foundlings to animal rescue centres.
1314.m: Young birds that fall rarely make it back.

1315.q: Your family is planning a day trip and thinking about how much money there is for it. What is a plan like this called?
1315.e: A budget is a plan of how much money you want to or can spend on something. That way you do not plan your money wrongly.

1316.q: What do the female common earwig’s pincers look like compared with the male’s?
a: They are longer than the body
1316.e: The female has pincers that are almost straight. This is how you can tell males and females apart.

1317.q: What do we call birds where some individuals migrate and others stay all year?
1317.e: The common buzzard is a partial migrant, because part of the population moves to warmer areas in winter while others stay in one place all year. This behaviour depends a lot on how much food there is.
1317.m: The common buzzard is a partial migrant.

1318.q: Which way does the opening of the pouch face in most female kangaroos?
1318.e: The pouch of most female kangaroos opens towards the front. That way the baby can easily climb in and look out.
1318.m: The kangaroo’s pouch opens at the front.

1319.q: Which wild bird are our domestic chickens descended from?
1319.e: All of today’s domestic chickens are descended from the wild red junglefowl, which lives in Southeast Asia. People tamed these wild birds a very long time ago.
1319.m: Domestic chickens come from the red junglefowl.

1320.q: What happens when the common wall lizard gets too cold?
a: It becomes sluggish and hardly moves
1320.e: Without enough warmth, the common wall lizard’s muscles lack energy. That is why it becomes slow and hardly moves in the cold.

1321.q: Where does a grasshopper like to live best?
a: In the snow on a mountain peak
1321.e: Grasshoppers need plants to eat and hide in. Meadows give them exactly that.

1322.q: Which predators can be dangerous to gibbons?
a: Big cats such as leopards, and snakes
1322.e: On the ground and in low trees, big cats or snakes can be dangerous to gibbons. High up in the treetops they are usually safer.

1323.q: Does a gorilla have a tail?
a: Yes, but only a short stump
Only the females have a tail
1323.e: Gorillas are great apes. Unlike most monkeys, great apes have no tail.

1324.q: Roughly how old can a bumblebee queen get?
1324.e: A bumblebee queen can live for about a year, because she also survives the winter. That is much longer than the life of a worker.
1324.m: Queens live for about a year.

1325.q: What is often on the striped hyena’s menu?
a: Carrion, but also fruit and small animals
1325.e: Striped hyenas are mainly scavengers. They also eat insects, small vertebrates and fruit.

1326.q: What is it called when you cut the wool off a sheep?
1326.e: Cutting off the wool is called shearing. It usually happens once a year, often in spring before it gets warm.

1327.q: Which kind of plant is the hippo’s main food?
1327.e: Hippos mainly eat grass that grows on land. At night they graze for hours in meadows near the river.
1327.m: Grass is the hippo’s favourite food.

1328.q: What does a squirrel do when it notices danger?
a: It escapes up a tree in a flash
It digs itself in at once
1328.e: When there is danger, the squirrel escapes up a tree in a flash. There it is safe from many enemies.
1328.m: When in danger, it escapes up a tree.

1329.q: Where does a puma mother usually give birth to her young?
a: In a sheltered cave or crack in the rocks
High up in a bird’s nest
In the middle of an open meadow
1329.e: The young are helpless at first. A hidden den protects them from enemies.
1329.m: Puma cubs are born in a hiding place.

1330.q: Roughly how big does an adult Syrian hamster get?
a: About as big as a hand
As big as a guinea pig
1330.e: An adult Syrian hamster is quite small and fits nicely in the palm of your hand. It stays much smaller than a guinea pig.

a: Introduced species that push out native plants
Plants that only grow in greenhouses
Plants that do not form flowers
1331.e: Some foreign plant species were brought in by humans and spread strongly. In doing so they often push out native plants and animals.
1331.m: Invasive species push out native plants.

1332.q: What is the name of Hans Christian Andersen’s famous fairy tale about a duckling?
1332.e: In this well-known fairy tale, a duckling is teased for a long time because it looks different. In the end it turns out that it is really a beautiful swan.
1332.m: The ugly duckling was a swan.

1333.q: Which animal carries pollen from flower to flower?
1333.e: Bees fly from flower to flower, carrying pollen with them. This helps the plants to form fruit.
1333.m: Bees pollinate flowers as they fly.

1334.q: What happens if trout have to live in badly polluted water?
a: They run into problems and can die
It does not bother them at all
1334.e: Trout are very sensitive and need clean water with lots of oxygen. In polluted water they can get ill or die.
1334.m: Polluted water is dangerous for trout.

1335.q: How do many reindeer in Scandinavia live today?
a: They belong to herders but roam freely on huge pastures
They all live in cramped sheds
They live only in zoos now
None of them have owners and they are completely wild
1335.e: Many reindeer in Scandinavia belong to herders, for example Sámi families. But they roam freely on huge pastures. This is called reindeer herding.

1336.q: What do young common buzzards in the nest mainly get to eat?
a: Mostly small rodents such as voles
1336.e: The parents mainly bring mice and other small prey to the young in the nest. This protein-rich food makes the chicks grow fast.
1336.m: The young mainly eat small rodents.

1337.q: Where does the stag beetle get its name from?
a: Its large jaws look like antlers
It lives only in deer sheds
It eats the fur of stags
It is as big as a young stag
1337.e: The males have greatly enlarged jaws that look like a stag’s antlers. The stag beetle belongs to the stag beetle family.
1337.m: The stag beetle’s jaws look like antlers.

1338.q: What do you find if you compare the bearded vulture’s eating habits with other vultures?
a: It is more specialised in bones
1338.e: While other vultures mainly eat meat from carcasses, the bearded vulture has specialised in bones and bone marrow. Hardly any other bird shares this special niche.
1338.m: The bearded vulture is a bone specialist.

1339.q: Why can you see things in the dark with a torch?
a: The light is thrown back from the things to your eyes
The torch makes the things glow by themselves
Your eyes then glow by themselves
1339.e: The light from the torch hits objects and is thrown back from them into your eyes. This is how you can see what is in front of you.
1339.m: We see things by reflected light.

a: Yes, males sing only in summer
1340.e: In most songbirds, only the males sing. But in robins the females sing too, especially in winter.

1341.q: Roughly how old can wild wolves get?
1341.e: In the wild, wolves usually live 8 to 13 years, but they often die earlier from illness or accidents. In human care they can live a little longer.
1341.m: Wild wolves usually live 8 to 13 years.

1342.q: What can gorillas do because they are very clever?
1342.e: Gorillas are very clever animals. Some learn to use simple tools such as sticks or to understand signs.

1343.q: Which special liquid do beavers produce from glands, which was also used as a scent in the past?
1343.e: Castoreum comes from special glands of the beaver and was used to mark its territory. In the past, people also used it as a medicine and in perfumes.

1344.q: How is the swift’s flight most different from a swallow’s?
a: It looks stiffer and faster, with sickle-shaped wings
It flies much more slowly than a swallow
1344.e: Swifts beat their wings less often but more strongly than swallows. This makes their flight look stiffer and at the same time very fast.
1344.m: Its flight looks stiff but very fast.

1345.q: What is special about the way the slow worm eats snails?
a: It swallows the prey whole or in big pieces
It chews it for a very long time
1345.e: It holds its prey with its small, backward-curving teeth. Then it swallows it down.

1346.q: How long does an adult garden cross spider usually live?
1346.e: Most garden cross spiders live only about a year. They hatch in spring and often die in autumn or winter.
1346.m: It usually lives only a year.

1347.q: What colour is a stone marten’s fur usually?
1347.e: The stone marten’s fur is usually greyish brown, which gives it good camouflage. Only the patch on its throat stands out white.
1347.m: Stone martens have greyish brown fur.

1348.q: What do storks use to find their way on their long flight south?
a: Landscapes, the sun and their experience
They just set off at random
Only the smell of the sea
1348.e: Storks find their way using rivers, mountains and coasts, the position of the sun and their experience. This lets them make the long journey to Africa and back.
1348.m: Storks find their way by landscape and sun.

1349.q: What does the red kite’s typical call sound like?
a: A loud croak like a crow
1349.e: The red kite’s call sounds like a high, drawn-out wee-wee-wee. You hear it especially when the bird circles over its territory.
1349.m: The red kite’s call is high and mournful.

1350.q: What does a cat need its whiskers for?
a: To sense obstacles and distances in the dark
1350.e: The whiskers, also called feelers, are very sensitive and help the cat find its way even in the dark. They sense the tiniest movements of air.

1352.q: What does a roe deer eat in winter when there is less fresh green food?
a: Twigs, buds and bark from trees
1352.e: In winter, fresh grass is rare. Then roe deer mainly eat twigs, buds and sometimes tree bark.
1352.m: In winter roe deer eat twigs and buds.

1353.q: How many times a year can a blackbird raise young?
a: Never more than once a year
1353.e: A blackbird can raise young several times in spring and summer. Often two or three broods grow up each year.
1353.m: Blackbirds often breed several times a year.

1354.q: What does a male common toad do when another male grabs hold of it?
a: It gives a short release call
It croaks loudly like a water frog
It puffs itself up and bites
1354.e: If a male is grabbed by another male by mistake, it gives a short call. This shows that it is not a female.
1354.m: The male defends itself with a release call.

1355.q: Apart from its lungs, how else does the adult alpine newt breathe on land?
1355.e: Like many amphibians, the alpine newt can also take in oxygen through its moist skin. This adds to its breathing with lungs.
1355.m: Alpine newts also breathe through their skin.

1356.q: Roughly how much does an adult alpaca weigh?
1356.e: Alpacas usually weigh between 50 and 80 kilograms. That makes them much lighter than llamas.

1357.q: How does the common frog often spend the winter?
a: It buries itself in mud or under leaves
It builds a nest in a tree
It moves to a cave high in the mountains
1357.e: In winter, the common frog often hides in the mud at the bottom of a pond or on land under leaves and moss. There it rests through the winter.
1357.m: Common frogs spend the winter in mud or leaves.

1358.q: What does a beaver mainly build its dam with?
1358.e: Beavers gnaw off branches and twigs and wedge them together with mud and stones to make a strong dam. This turns streams and rivers into small ponds.
1358.m: Dams are made of branches and mud.

1359.q: What body shape does the adder have?
a: Very thin and several metres long
1359.e: Compared with grass snakes, it looks thick and short. Its tail is short and ends in a point.

1360.q: How many dorsal fins does a perch have?
1360.e: The perch has two separate dorsal fins, one behind the other. This is a typical feature of perches.
1360.m: The perch has two dorsal fins.

1362.q: What can you use to lift heavy stones more easily?
1362.e: A lever spreads the force so that you do not have to push as hard. Even a long pole can help to move a heavy stone.
1362.m: A lever makes heavy work easier.

1366.q: Which animals can be seen on the coat of arms of the canton of Thurgau?
1366.e: The coat of arms of the canton of Thurgau is divided diagonally into white and green and shows two golden lions standing upright. It goes back to the Counts of Kyburg.
1366.m: Thurgau has two lions on its coat of arms.

1387.q: What is the pilgrimage to Mecca called, which Muslims should make once in their life?
1387.e: The Hajj is one of the Five Pillars of Islam. Every year millions of Muslims travel to Mecca to make this pilgrimage.
1387.m: The Hajj is the pilgrimage to Mecca.

1417.q: How many ventricles and atria does the human heart have altogether?
1417.e: The heart has four chambers: two atria and two ventricles. Together they keep the blood circulating around the body.

1418.q: What happens to the falling speed of objects when there is no air resistance?
a: Objects do not fall at all
1418.e: Without air resistance, gravity accelerates all bodies equally, no matter how heavy they are. You can see this in a vacuum, for example, when a feather and a hammer fall equally fast.
1418.m: In a vacuum, all things fall equally fast.

1433.q: What is meant by ecological succession?
a: The step-by-step development of a habitat
The sudden extinction of a species
1433.e: After a forest fire or on unused land, different plant species settle one after another until a stable forest forms. This process is called succession.
1433.m: Succession describes the development of a habitat.

1448.q: What is meant by a “developing country”?
a: A country that is less developed economically and socially than rich industrial states
A country that does not yet have its own government
A country that may not have members in the UN
A country that consists of only one city
1448.e: Developing countries often have less wealth, education or health care than industrial countries such as Switzerland. International organisations support such countries through development cooperation.
1448.m: Developing countries are economically less strong.

1453.q: Which large bird of prey was wiped out in the Swiss Alps and has been successfully reintroduced since the 1990s?
1453.e: People wrongly believed the bearded vulture to be dangerous and therefore wiped it out. Since 1991 it has been deliberately released back into the Alps.
1453.m: The bearded vulture is returning to the Alps.

1454.q: What is a household account book?
a: A record of all income and spending, to keep track of your money
An official document from the municipality
A savings account for the whole family
1454.e: In a household account book you write down how much money comes in and what you spend it on. That way you can see where the money goes and plan better.
1454.m: A household account book shows where money goes.

1457.q: How does a leopard mark its territory?
a: With scent marks and scratch marks
1457.e: Leopards use urine and scents and scratch trees. That way other leopards know the area is taken.
1457.m: Leopards mark with scent and scratch marks.

a: An envelope in which you send your ballot paper by post
1462.e: If you don't want to go to the ballot box in person, you put your completed ballot paper in a voting envelope. It is then sent by post.
1462.m: The ballot paper travels by post in the voting envelope.

1476.q: Where does the lake trout, a relative of the brown trout, live?
a: In large lakes, swimming up inflowing rivers to spawn
1476.e: The lake trout grows up in large, deep lakes. To spawn, it swims into streams and rivers.
1476.m: Lake trout spawn in rivers flowing into the lake.

1478.q: Why are wild dogs sometimes hunted by farmers?
a: Because people fear they kill livestock
1478.e: Some people fear for their livestock and therefore hunt wild dogs. This is one reason why their numbers are falling.
1478.m: Conflicts with people threaten wild dogs.

1491.q: What is the force called that pulls a vehicle down a sloping road?
1491.e: On a slope, part of the force of gravity pulls the vehicle down along the slope. The steeper the road, the greater this downhill force.
1491.m: On slopes, the downhill force pulls things downwards.

1496.q: What is a meteor, also called a “shooting star”?
a: A piece of rock that burns up in the atmosphere
1496.e: Small rocks from space enter the Earth’s atmosphere at high speed and burn up. The bright streak of light is also called a shooting star.
1496.m: A shooting star is a piece of rock burning up.

1513.q: What are the “bilateral agreements” between Switzerland and the EU?
a: A series of separate agreements instead of EU membership
1513.e: Because Switzerland is not an EU member, it has instead made many separate agreements with the EU, for example on the free movement of people or on trade. These govern cooperation in important areas.
1513.m: Bilateral agreements govern cooperation between Switzerland and the EU one area at a time.

1546.q: What is the device called that you can use in a forest to find out where north is?
1546.e: A compass has a needle that lines up like a small magnet. It always points to the Earth's magnetic north pole.

1555.q: A trout's skin feels slippery. What is the layer of slime for?
a: It stores food for the winter
1555.e: The slime protects the skin from germs and makes the fish smooth. That is why you should always hold fish with wet hands.
1555.m: The slime protects the fish's skin.

1566.q: What does abuse of power mean?
a: When someone uses their power to harm others.
When laws apply equally to everyone.
1566.e: Abuse of power happens when a person uses their position to enrich themselves unlawfully or to oppress others. It is especially common in dictatorships, because nobody checks the power.
1566.m: Power without checks is often abused.

1572.q: In which unit is electrical energy usually measured in the home?
1572.e: The kilowatt-hour shows how much energy an appliance uses over a certain time. The electricity meter at home measures exactly this value.
1572.m: Electricity use is measured in kilowatt-hours.

1578.q: What is the rule in Switzerland about health insurance?
a: Everyone who lives in Switzerland must take out basic insurance with a health insurance company
Only adults have to be insured
The state automatically pays all medical costs
1578.e: In Switzerland health insurance is compulsory: everyone must take out basic insurance, which they have to pay for themselves. This means monthly premiums in the family budget.
1578.m: Health insurance is compulsory in Switzerland.

1585.q: What does a climate graph show for a place?
a: Temperature and precipitation over the whole year
Only the height above sea level
1585.e: A climate graph shows the average temperature and amount of precipitation for each month at a place. That way you can see the typical climate at a glance.
1585.m: Climate graphs show temperature and precipitation.

1586.q: What does the leopard need its long tail for?
1586.e: The long tail helps the leopard keep its balance, especially on branches. It is about two thirds as long as the body.

1595.q: What is the headscarf that some Muslim women wear called?
1595.e: Some Muslim women wear a headscarf for religious reasons, called a hijab. It covers the hair, not the face.
1595.m: The hijab is a Muslim headscarf.

1596.q: What does a common raven mainly eat?
a: almost anything, for example carrion, small animals, eggs and fruit
1596.e: The common raven is a typical omnivore and adapts its diet to whatever is available. Carrion is especially important for it.

1597.q: Are there dolphins that live in rivers?
a: Yes, for example in the Amazon
No, dolphins only live in the sea
No, they would freeze in a river
1597.e: As well as ocean dolphins, there are river dolphins, for example in the Amazon in South America. They live in fresh water.

1598.q: What do alpacas often do when they feel threatened or annoyed?
1598.e: Alpacas spit to defend themselves against other alpacas or troublemakers. Sometimes stomach contents come flying out too.
1598.m: Alpacas spit when they are annoyed.

1599.q: Who looks after the young in cheetahs?
1599.e: In cheetahs, the mother raises the young completely on her own. The males do not help.
1599.m: Cheetah mothers raise their cubs alone.

1600.q: How are a jackal's claws different from a cat's?
1600.e: Dogs have claws that always stay out. Cats can pull their claws in.

1601.q: Which parts of plants does the wood mouse also like to eat?
1601.e: As well as seeds and nuts, the wood mouse also likes fresh buds and young plant shoots.
1601.m: Buds are on the menu too.

1602.q: Does a jellyfish have a brain?
a: Only when it is grown up
1602.e: Jellyfish have no brain, just a simple net of nerves. Even so, they can react to light and touch.

1603.q: Why do edible dormice sometimes spend the winter together in small groups?
1603.e: Several dormice lying close together can warm each other. This saves energy during the cold winter months.

1604.q: Roughly how big is the territory of a pair of tawny owls?
a: It usually covers several hectares of woodland or built-up area
It is as small as a garden bed
Tawny owls never have their own territory
1604.e: A pair of tawny owls defends a territory of usually several hectares, where they hunt and breed. The exact size depends on how much food there is.
1604.m: A tawny owl territory covers several hectares.

1605.q: How well can sheep walk in the mountains?
a: Very sure-footedly, even on steep slopes
Very badly, they often fall over
They can only walk on flat ground
They need help from people to do it
1605.e: Sheep are very sure-footed and can climb well even on steep mountain slopes. Their hooves help them not to slip.
1605.m: Sheep climb safely in the mountains.

1607.q: What is typical of the ears of many kinds of marten?
a: They are rather small and rounded
They are huge like a hare's
Martens have no ears at all
They are pointed and very long like a bat's
1607.e: Many kinds of marten have rather small, rounded ears that lie close to the head. This suits their life in narrow tunnels, burrows and holes in trees.
1607.m: Marten ears are small and round.

1608.q: What is it called when a red deer feeds on fresh plants?
1608.e: When a deer feeds on leaves, shoots and plants, it is called browsing. The word is used for many wild animals.

1609.q: Why are there many different kinds of whitefish in Switzerland?
a: Separate species developed in many lakes
They were all brought in from the sea
They were bred in a laboratory
Each river has exactly one species
1609.e: After the last Ice Age, whitefish lived in many separate lakes. Over time, separate species developed there that differ in size and food.
1609.m: Many lakes have their own whitefish species.

1610.q: Which national park in the USA is famous for its wild bison?
1610.e: One of the largest wild bison herds in the USA lives in Yellowstone National Park. Visitors often see them near the road.
1610.m: Yellowstone is famous for bison herds.

1611.q: What does a very small baby starfish look like?
a: Completely different from an adult starfish
Exactly the same as a big starfish
1611.e: Young starfish look completely different from their parents at first. Only later do they get the familiar star shape.
1611.m: Babies look different from their parents.

1612.q: What is soft chamois leather often used for?
1612.e: Chamois leather is very soft and soaks up water well. That is why people use it to clean windows, cars and glasses without scratching them.
1612.m: Chamois leather is soft and absorbent.

1613.q: What colour is a pike's belly usually?
1613.e: A pike's back is dark, but its belly is light and whitish. This is good camouflage, both from below and from above.
1613.m: A pike's belly is light coloured.

1614.q: What colour is the flesh of some trout often, depending on what they eat?
1614.e: Some trout eat small crustaceans that contain certain colourings. This can make their flesh pink to orange.
1614.m: Trout flesh can be pink or orange.

1615.q: What is the young jellyfish polyp usually attached to?
a: A stone or rock on the seabed
1615.e: The polyp sits firmly on stones or rocks on the seabed. From there it can later split into many small jellyfish.
1615.m: The polyp sits fixed on stones.

1616.q: Which shark has stripes on its skin like a big cat?
1616.e: The tiger shark has dark stripes on its skin, similar to a tiger. Young tiger sharks especially show these patterns clearly.
1616.m: The tiger shark has striped skin.

1617.q: What does a lake trout usually look like in a lake?
1617.e: In a lake, the lake trout often looks silvery. It has dark spots on its body and head.

1618.q: Which god of ancient Egypt is shown with the head of a jackal?
1618.e: Anubis has a jackal's head on a human body. He is one of the gods of the dead.

1619.q: What is a group of hippos called?
1619.e: Hippos often live together in a herd in the water. A herd can be made up of several animals.

1620.q: Why do you rarely see moles above ground?
a: They spend almost their whole life underground
Because they only exist at night
Because there are very few of them
1620.e: Moles rarely leave their tunnels because they are in danger on the surface. That is why you hardly ever see them.

1621.q: What are avalanche dogs in the Swiss Alps specially trained for?
a: To find people buried under snow
To set off avalanches on purpose
1621.e: Avalanche dogs are trained to use their sensitive noses to track down people under masses of snow. They are often used in mountain rescue in Switzerland.
1621.m: Avalanche dogs find people buried in snow.

1622.q: The Roman snail is a hermaphrodite. What happens after mating?
1622.e: Because both partners have male and female organs, both can lay eggs after mating. So there are two clutches of eggs at once.

1623.q: Roughly how fast can a kangaroo hop?
1623.e: A kangaroo can hop very fast, almost as fast as a car in town. Its strong legs make this possible.

1624.q: What colour is the coat of the Appenzell goat?
1624.e: The Appenzell goat has a completely white coat and usually no horns. It comes from the Appenzell region.

1625.q: Which statement about the growth of the wels catfish is true?
a: It stops growing after one year
1625.e: Like many fish, the wels catfish grows throughout its life, but most strongly when young. That is why old fish reach impressive sizes.
1625.m: Fish often grow throughout their lives.

1626.q: What is the colourful Hindu festival called, where people throw coloured powder at each other?
1626.e: At the Holi festival Hindus celebrate spring. People cheerfully throw colourful powder and water at each other.
1626.m: Holi is the colourful festival of colours.

1627.q: Where does the Syrian brown bear live?
a: In Western Asia, for example in Turkey and Iran
1627.e: The Syrian brown bear is a subspecies of the brown bear and lives in parts of Western Asia. It is usually a bit smaller and lighter in colour than European brown bears.
1627.m: The Syrian brown bear lives in Western Asia.

1628.q: What is typical of the shape of a dolphin's body?
1628.e: A dolphin's body is long and slim. This shape helps it glide through the water quickly and with little resistance.

1629.q: Why are fruit and vegetables healthy?
a: They provide vitamins your body needs
1629.e: Fruit and vegetables contain lots of vitamins and minerals. The body needs them to work properly.
1629.m: Fruit and vegetables make you strong.

1631.q: Why can't pond skaters walk on a glass of soapy water?
1631.e: Soap makes the water surface less able to carry weight. Then the legs get wet and the pond skater sinks.

1632.q: Where does a wild goose normally build its nest?
a: On the ground, well hidden near water
Floating in the middle of the water
1632.e: Wild geese usually build their nests from grass and their own feathers right on the ground. They look for a well-hidden spot close to water.
1632.m: Goose nests are hidden on the ground.

1633.q: What do common ravens often show in acrobatic flights during courtship?
a: Loops and other daring flying moves
they only ever fly straight ahead
1633.e: Common ravens are known for their impressive flying skills, especially during courtship. They do loops and even fly upside down for short stretches.
1633.m: Courtship flights with loops and tricks.

1634.q: Why shouldn't pet rabbits live alone?
a: They are social animals and need company
They always become aggressive in groups
1634.e: Rabbits naturally live in groups and need other rabbits to feel good. Rabbits kept alone are often sad and bored.

1635.q: In which famous African national park do many rhinos live?
1635.e: Kruger National Park in South Africa is one of the most important protected areas for rhinos in Africa. Many wild animals live there under protection.
1635.m: Many rhinos live in Kruger National Park.

1636.q: What colour are the legs of the white stork?
1636.e: The long legs of the white stork are red. It uses them to stride through meadows and water.

1637.q: What happens to the shell of a Roman snail as it grows?
1637.e: The shell grows along with the snail. It is never shed like an old piece of clothing.
1637.m: The shell grows with the snail.

1638.q: Which large group of animals does the ant belong to?
1638.e: The ant has six legs and a body divided into parts. That makes it an insect.

1640.q: What kind of diet does the puma have?
1640.e: Pumas feed only on meat. This includes hoofed animals but also smaller prey.

1641.q: What is a grasshopper especially good at?
1641.e: Grasshoppers have strong back legs. With them they can make huge jumps.

1642.q: What does a young cockerel chick hatch from?
1642.e: Like all chickens, a cockerel hatches from an egg as a chick. The hen sits on the egg for about three weeks.

1643.q: How many different bird species does the cuckoo use as hosts around the world?
1643.e: Worldwide, the cuckoo can use over 100 different bird species as hosts for its eggs. But each female cuckoo usually specialises in one particular species.
1643.m: The cuckoo uses many different host birds.

1644.q: How does a mother sheep recognise her own lamb in the flock?
a: By its smell and its voice
By the colour of its ears
1644.e: A mother sheep recognises her lamb by its smell and by its voice when it bleats. That way she can find her lamb even in a big flock.
1644.m: Mother sheep recognise lambs by smell.

1645.q: Why is life getting harder for the barn swallow in Switzerland?
a: Because modern barns often have no way in and there are fewer insects
Because there is too much rain
Because summers have become too short
Because there are too many trees
1645.e: Modern, sealed barns often no longer give the barn swallow a way in to nest. On top of that, it is struggling because there are fewer flying insects to eat.
1645.m: Fewer insects and nest sites harm it.

1646.q: What does a common toad like to eat most?
1646.e: The common toad feeds on small animals such as insects, worms and snails. That is why it is very useful in the garden.
1646.m: Common toads hunt insects and snails.

1647.q: What role does the male golden eagle usually take during the breeding season?
a: It often brings food for the female sitting on the eggs
It sits on the eggs alone the whole time
It leaves the territory completely during breeding
It builds a second nest during breeding
1647.e: While the female sits on the eggs for most of the breeding season, the male often does the hunting and brings food to the nest. So both parents work together.
1647.m: The male feeds the female on the eggs.

1648.q: What do cheetahs have on their faces that look like black lines under the eyes?
1648.e: The black lines from the eye to the mouth are called tear marks. They are thought to stop the sun from dazzling them, a bit like with athletes.
1648.m: Tear marks protect against sun glare.

1649.q: What does the great spotted woodpecker sometimes drum on in towns?
1649.e: Metal sounds even louder than wood. That is why in towns it sometimes uses metal to make a loud drumming noise.

1650.q: Roughly how long is a mole's pregnancy?
1650.e: After mating, the mother mole carries her young in her belly for about four weeks. Then the tiny babies are born.

1651.q: What happens in a short circuit?
a: The current flows along a very short path with little resistance and becomes very strong
1651.e: In a short circuit, the positive and negative terminals are connected directly without enough resistance in between. A very large current can then flow and produce heat, which can be dangerous.
1651.m: In a short circuit, too much current flows along a short path.

1652.q: Which parts of the badger's body are built to be especially strong for digging?
a: The front paws with strong claws
1652.e: The badger has especially powerful front paws with long claws. With them it easily digs long tunnels in the ground.
1652.m: Strong front paws are the badger's tools.

1653.q: What can the praying mantis do with its head that many other insects can't do so well?
a: Throw it off and grow it back
1653.e: Its head sits on a flexible neck. So it can look around without moving its body.

1654.q: What are the red flaps of skin under a chicken's beak called?
1654.e: The red wattles hang down under the chicken's chin. They help the chicken get rid of extra heat.

1655.q: Why is the African wild dog important for its ecosystem?
a: It keeps the numbers of prey animals in balance
1655.e: As a predator, it mainly catches weak and sick animals. This keeps nature in balance.

1656.q: What does the badger do in winter to survive?
a: It lives off its fat reserves
It hunts much more than usual
It lays eggs in its sett
It travels far away to the sea
1656.e: In autumn, the badger eats until it has a thick layer of fat. It lives off this when there is little food to find in winter.
1656.m: Badgers live off fat in winter.

1657.q: Why is the peregrine falcon called a “peregrine”?
a: Because some peregrines travel long distances
Because it likes walking on the ground
Because it only nests near footpaths
Because it goes with hikers in the mountains
1657.e: “Peregrine” means wanderer. Many peregrines from the far north fly a long way south in winter, and young falcons also roam widely. That is where the name comes from.

1658.q: Why can an octopus squeeze through very narrow gaps?
1658.e: Because the octopus has no bones, it can squeeze its whole body together very tightly. So it fits through holes hardly bigger than its beak.
1658.m: With no bones, it fits through anything.

1659.q: What is the organ in the inner ear that is responsible for your balance called?
1659.e: In the inner ear, next to the cochlea, sits the balance organ. It tells the brain how your head is positioned in space.
1659.m: Your sense of balance sits in your inner ear.

1660.q: What role does the lake trout play as a predatory fish in a lake?
a: It helps keep the numbers of other fish in balance
It cleans salt out of the water
1660.e: Predatory fish eat prey fish and so control their numbers. This helps keep the lake's ecosystem stable.
1660.m: Predatory fish keep the lake in balance.

1661.q: How well can young brown bears climb?
a: Young bears often climb better than adult bears
Young bears can't climb at all
1661.e: Young brown bears often climb more skilfully than adults because they are lighter and more agile. As they get heavier, climbing becomes harder for them.
1661.m: Young bears are especially good climbers.

1662.q: Which country has the largest population of brown bears today?
1662.e: Russia is home to by far the most brown bears in the world. Its huge forests and mountain areas give the animals lots of space.
1662.m: Russia has the most brown bears.

1663.q: What colour are the back feathers of an adult kestrel usually?
1663.e: The kestrel's back is usually reddish brown with small dark spots. This colouring also helps it hide in open country.
1663.m: Its back is reddish brown with spots.

1664.q: Why are many gardeners happy to see earwigs?
a: Because they loosen the soil like earthworms
1664.e: Aphids harm many plants. Earwigs help to keep their numbers down.
1664.m: Earwigs are useful helpers in the garden.

1665.q: What are the dromedary's small, hairy ears for?
1665.e: Hair in the ears holds sand back. So less of it gets into the ear.

1666.q: What role does the magpie often play in old European stories and legends?
a: It is often shown as a clever, sometimes cunning character
It is seen as especially stupid and slow
It is seen as a sacred animal that must not be touched
1666.e: In many old stories and fairy tales from Europe, the magpie is described as a clever, sometimes cunning animal. This reputation is also linked to its genuinely high intelligence.
1666.m: In stories, the magpie is clever.

1667.q: How does a sparrow's beak change in winter?
1667.e: In winter, the sparrow's beak becomes a little lighter and greyish brown instead of black. In spring it gets darker again.
1667.m: The beak gets lighter in winter.

1668.q: Which insect has colourful wings and used to be a caterpillar?
1668.e: A butterfly develops from a caterpillar that changes inside a pupa. Its wings often have colourful patterns.

1669.q: How big is a group of ring-tailed lemurs usually?
1669.e: Ring-tailed lemurs live in groups of males, females and young. Usually there are between five and thirty animals.

1670.q: How do elephants help other animals in Africa?
a: They dig water holes and spread seeds
1670.e: When they eat, elephants spread many plant seeds, and sometimes they dig water holes that other animals use too.

1671.q: How do lambs show that they are full of energy and happy?
1671.e: Young lambs often jump and leap happily around the field, especially when they are full and healthy. It looks very funny.

1672.q: Why do butterflies need colourful flower meadows?
a: There they find food and plants for their eggs
There they can sleep in winter
There they are protected from rain
There they drink water from puddles
1672.e: In colourful meadows, butterflies find nectar and the right plants for their caterpillars. Without such meadows, many species have hardly any chance of surviving.

1673.q: What should you do if you find a roe deer fawn lying alone in the woods?
a: Not touch it and leave it alone
1673.e: A fawn lying alone has usually not been abandoned; its mother is often nearby. So you should not touch it, so that it doesn't smell of people.
1673.m: Never touch a roe deer fawn.

1674.q: Where do bumblebees especially often build their nests?
a: In old mouse holes in the ground
In the middle of a pond
1674.e: Many kinds of bumblebee use abandoned mouse holes because they are already warm and sheltered. There the queen lays her first eggs.
1674.m: Bumblebee nests are often in mouse holes.

1675.q: Which beetle was sacred in ancient Egypt?
1675.e: The Egyptians saw the rolling beetle as a picture of the sun moving across the sky. The scarab was worn as an amulet.
1675.m: The scarab was sacred in ancient Egypt.

1676.q: Why does a least weasel have to eat very often?
a: Because it can go months without food
Because it only eats once a week
Because it needs hardly any energy
1676.e: Small animals lose heat faster for their body size and burn more energy. That is why the least weasel has to hunt regularly.

1677.q: What is typical of how kestrels raise their young, compared with many other birds?
a: Both parents help to look after the young
Only other birds look after the young
The young look after themselves completely from day one
The father disappears for ever right after the eggs are laid
1677.e: Both males and females help to raise the young. While the female does more brooding and feeding at first, the male brings the prey.
1677.m: Both parents look after the young.

1678.q: Which saint is the big cathedral in Solothurn named after?
1678.e: According to legend, Saint Ursus lived in Solothurn a long time ago. The town's big cathedral was named in his honour.
1678.m: The cathedral is named after Saint Ursus.

1679.q: Which group of animals do guinea pigs belong to?
1679.e: Like all rodents, guinea pigs have teeth that keep growing, which they use for gnawing. They belong to the order of rodents.

1680.q: How does the bearded vulture usually fly to save energy?
a: It glides for a long time without flapping
It always flies very low over the ground
1680.e: Thanks to its large wings, the bearded vulture uses rising air in the mountains to glide for hours. So it hardly has to flap and saves a lot of energy.
1680.m: The bearded vulture glides instead of flapping.

1681.q: What makes the ibex's hooves so special for climbing?
a: They have a hard rim and a soft, grippy sole
They have suction pads like a gecko
They are armed with small claws
They are covered in fur like snowshoes
1681.e: The ibex's hooves have a hard outer rim for stability and a soft sole that moulds itself to the rock. So the animals find a safe hold even on the steepest rock faces.
1681.m: Hard rim, soft sole, perfect for climbing.

1682.q: What does a penguin like to eat most?
a: Fish and small sea creatures such as krill
1682.e: Penguins catch their food in the water. They eat fish, squid and small crustaceans such as krill.

1683.q: Why does the polar bear have big paws?
a: So that it doesn't sink into the snow
1683.e: The big paws spread the polar bear's weight over the snow and ice. So it doesn't sink in so easily.
1683.m: Big paws help on the ice.

1684.q: In which season do you see the first bumblebee queens flying?
a: Never, they only fly at night
1684.e: As soon as it gets warmer in spring, the queens wake up from hibernation. You often see them flying around looking for a place to nest.

1685.q: Which bird is a close relative of the common raven?
1685.e: The common raven, carrion crow and rook belong to the same genus. They differ mainly in size and calls.
1685.m: Ravens and crows are closely related.

1686.q: Which penguin species lives furthest north, even close to the equator?
1686.e: The Galápagos penguin lives on the Galápagos Islands, which lie close to the equator. It is the only penguin species found that far north.
1686.m: The Galápagos penguin lives almost on the equator.

1687.q: What is the smaller relative of the house sparrow with a brown cap called?
1687.e: The tree sparrow is related to the house sparrow but has a brown crown and a black spot on its cheek. It lives more in the countryside than in towns.
1687.m: The tree sparrow has a brown head.

1688.q: Roughly how old can a pet cat get?
1688.e: If they are well looked after, pet cats often live to 15 to 20 years. Some get even older.
1688.m: Pet cats can live 15 to 20 years.

1689.q: How do kangaroos cool down on hot days?
a: They lick their front legs wet
They sweat all over their bodies
1689.e: On hot days, kangaroos lick their front legs wet with saliva. When the saliva dries, it cools their body.
1689.m: Kangaroos lick themselves to cool down.

1690.q: Why is it a good thing that guinea pigs' teeth keep growing?
a: Because they are constantly worn down by chewing
Because they need new teeth in winter
Because they use them to dig holes
1690.e: Gnawing and chewing hay makes the teeth a little shorter all the time. That is why they keep growing.
1690.m: Guinea pig teeth grow throughout life.

1691.q: What is an important job of the mute swan's webbed feet?
1691.e: The webbing between the toes works like small paddles. This lets the swan move powerfully through the water.
1691.m: Webbed feet work like small paddles.

1692.q: Roughly how long is the spotted hyena's pregnancy?
1692.e: Pregnancy lasts about 110 days, a little more than three months. Usually one or two young are born.
1692.m: Spotted hyenas are pregnant for just over three months.

1693.q: How big is a pack of African wild dogs usually?
1693.e: A pack usually has about 6 to 20 animals. Sometimes there are more.
1693.m: A pack usually has 6 to 20 animals.

1694.q: What job does the common wall lizard's tongue have as well as tasting?
a: It helps it sense smells in the air
It works as a fin for swimming
It is only used for digging
1694.e: The tongue collects tiny scent particles from the air. These are passed to a sense organ in the roof of the mouth.

1695.q: What other name is the African wild dog also known by?
1695.e: It is also called the painted wolf or painted dog because of its patchy coat. It is not related to hyenas, even though it looks a little like one.

1696.q: How do the legs of the golden eagle look different from those of the white-tailed eagle?
a: They are feathered right down to the toes
1696.e: In the golden eagle, the legs are completely feathered down to the toes, but in the white-tailed eagle they are not. This feature helps to tell the two species apart.
1696.m: Golden eagle legs are feathered to the toes.

1697.q: What is the top speed of a cheetah?
1697.e: The cheetah is the fastest land animal in the world. Over short distances it reaches up to 100 km/h.
1697.m: The cheetah is the fastest land animal.

1698.q: Which animals can be dangerous for a dolphin?
1698.e: Large sharks sometimes hunt dolphins too, especially young or sick ones. Healthy adult dolphins, however, can often defend themselves well.

1699.q: What colour are a kestrel's legs and feet usually?
1699.e: The kestrel's legs and feet are a striking yellow. The claws, on the other hand, are dark and sharp.

1700.q: Which two feather colours are found in tawny owls?
a: A grey and a reddish-brown form
1700.e: Tawny owls come in two colour forms, a rather grey one and a rather rusty brown one. Both help them hide in the woods.
1700.m: Tawny owls come in grey or brown.

1701.q: How many eggs does a barn owl usually lay?
1701.e: A barn owl normally lays four to seven eggs. When there are lots of mice, it can be more.
1701.m: It usually lays four to seven eggs.

1702.q: What is a “COP” in connection with climate protection?
a: An annual United Nations world climate conference
An abbreviation for police in international organisations
1702.e: At the COP (Conference of the Parties), representatives of almost every state meet to negotiate measures against climate change. The Paris Climate Agreement, for example, was decided there.
1702.m: The COP is the UN world climate conference.

1703.q: What does the budgie need its strong, curved beak for?
1703.e: With its strong beak, the budgie cracks hard seed husks. It also helps it climb on branches and cage bars.
1703.m: The beak is for cracking and climbing.

1704.q: What is the greatest age a common swift can reach in the wild?
1704.e: Although many young birds don't survive their first year, some swifts can get amazingly old. In studies, some reached an age of over 20 years.

1705.q: What is the best-known courtship ritual of the great crested grebe called, in which the birds rise up breast to breast?
1705.e: In the penguin dance, both birds rise up out of the water and face each other breast to breast. They often shake water weed together as they do so.
1705.m: The penguin dance is the most famous courtship ritual.

1706.q: What else do chamois eat in winter when few green plants grow?
1706.e: In winter, fresh green plants are scarce, so chamois also eat buds, moss and bark from bushes. This helps them get through the cold season.
1706.m: In winter, chamois eat buds and bark.

1707.q: What is a rhino's horn made of?
a: The same material as our hair and nails
1707.e: A rhino's horn is made of the same material as our fingernails and hair. It is not made of bone.
1707.m: Rhino horn is like our fingernails.

1708.q: What does a mother hippo do to protect her calf?
a: She always stays very close and defends it
She leaves it alone in the water
She hides it in a tree
She gives it to other animals to look after
1708.e: Mother hippos are very caring and stay close to their calf. When there is danger, they bravely defend it against enemies.
1708.m: Mother hippos always protect their calf.

1709.q: Can a ring-tailed lemur hold on to branches with its tail?
a: No, the tail is for balance and signals
Yes, it is a strong gripping tail
Yes, it hangs upside down from it for hours
No, it has no tail muscles at all
1709.e: The ring-tailed lemur does not have a gripping tail like some monkeys in South America. Its tail helps it balance and is used for communication.
1709.m: The lemur's tail balances and signals.

1710.q: What does the name “ring-tailed lemur” describe?
1710.e: The ring-tailed lemur is named after its tail with black and white rings. The name describes its most striking feature.
1710.m: The ringed tail gives the lemur its name.

1711.q: How do many pond skaters behave on a pond?
a: They are often found in groups
They only live alone in caves
They only hunt at night in swarms
1711.e: You often see several of them on the water at the same time. They share a good hunting spot.
1711.m: You often see several together on the water.

1712.q: What does a seahorse like to eat most?
1712.e: Seahorses suck in small crustaceans such as water fleas with their tube-shaped mouths. They do this again and again all day long.

1713.q: In which waters does the alpine newt prefer to lay its eggs?
a: In calm pools and small ponds
1713.e: The alpine newt prefers still, small waters without fish for laying its eggs. There the eggs and larvae are better protected from predators.
1713.m: Calm pools are ideal for laying eggs.

1714.q: Why is bread not good food for hedgehogs?
a: It is hard for them to digest
It is too small for them
1714.e: Bread swells up in the hedgehog's stomach and is hard for it to digest. Cat food or special hedgehog food, for example, is better.
1714.m: Bread is hard for hedgehogs to digest.

1715.q: Roughly how many eggs can a female mosquito lay at once?
1715.e: A female mosquito often lays several hundred eggs at once in water. A great many small larvae then hatch from them.

1716.q: Roughly how often does a pair of sparrows breed in a year?
1716.e: Sparrows can raise chicks two or three times a year. So their numbers grow quite quickly.
1716.m: Sparrows often breed several times a year.

1717.q: What is the hedgehog species that lives here in Switzerland called?
1717.e: The hedgehog that lives in Switzerland is the European hedgehog, also called the West European hedgehog. It is the most common hedgehog species in Europe.
1717.m: The European hedgehog lives in Switzerland.

1718.q: How often does a mute swan usually breed in a year?
1718.e: Mute swans normally have young only once a year. This usually happens in spring.
1718.m: Young are born once a year.

1719.q: What does the Latin word “lacustris” in the lake trout's name mean?
1719.e: The word comes from “lacus”, the Latin word for lake. It shows that this trout lives in lakes.
1719.m: The Latin word “lacustris” means “belonging to a lake”.

1720.q: In which canton is the Swiss National Park, where many ibex live under protection?
1720.e: The Swiss National Park is in the Engadine in the canton of the Grisons. Ibex have lived there for many decades.
1720.m: The National Park in the Engadine protects ibex.

1721.q: Who feeds the carrion crow's chicks in the nest?
a: only other birds from the neighbourhood
nobody, the chicks find food themselves straight away
1721.e: Both the male and the female help to feed the hungry chicks in the nest. They take turns bringing food.
1721.m: Both parents feed the crow chicks.

1722.q: What does wolves' fur often look like, depending on the region?
a: It can be grey, brown, black or white
It is always striped like a tiger's
1722.e: The colour of wolves' fur varies with where they live, from grey and brown to black or almost white. In Switzerland, most wolves are greyish brown.
1722.m: Wolf fur varies a lot in colour.

1723.q: What helps the jaguar hunt at night?
a: Very good eyes and sharp hearing
1723.e: Like other cats, the jaguar sees very well even in low light. It also has sharp hearing and quiet paws.
1723.m: Jaguars see and hear very well.

1724.q: In ring-tailed lemurs, who usually leaves the group they were born in?
1724.e: Young males later move to other groups. The females usually stay in the group they were born in.

1725.q: What role do man-made nest boxes play for common swifts in towns?
a: they replace lost natural gaps in buildings
they are mainly used as winter quarters in Africa
they are only used by young swifts for practice
they are completely unsuitable for swifts
1725.e: Because many old gaps in walls disappear when buildings are renovated, people put up nest boxes on houses on purpose. These give swifts an important replacement for lost natural nesting places.
1725.m: Nest boxes replace lost gaps in walls.

1726.q: Which cow is a typical Swiss cattle breed?
1726.e: Swiss Brown cattle are a well-known Swiss breed with brown coats. These cows give a lot of good milk.
1726.m: Swiss Brown is a Swiss cattle breed.

1728.q: What do alpine marmots like doing when the sun is shining?
a: They warm up sitting upright on rocks
They look for shade deep in the forest
They dig themselves in straight away
1728.e: On sunny days, marmots like to sit on a raised rock. There they can warm up and keep a lookout for danger at the same time.

1729.q: What do newly hatched sparrow chicks look like?
1729.e: When sparrow chicks hatch, they have no feathers yet and cannot see. So their parents have to take extra good care of them.
1729.m: Sparrow chicks start out naked and blind.

1730.q: What is special about a tapir's skin?
1730.e: The thick skin, especially on the neck, protects it from bites and thorns. This helps when it is attacked and when it moves through thick undergrowth.

1731.q: What colour are an eagle owl's eyes typically?
1731.e: The eagle owl's big eyes usually glow a strong orange. They help it see well even in low light.

1732.q: What happens to a seahorse's colour when it hides?
1732.e: Seahorses can change colour to camouflage themselves better. Then they look almost like the plants or corals around them.
1732.m: Its colour adapts to its surroundings.

1733.q: What can a seahorse do with its head that many other fish can't?
a: Bend it forward like a horse
1733.e: A seahorse's neck can bend slightly, almost like a horse's. Most other fish can't do this.

1734.q: Which word best describes how martens feed?
1734.e: Martens are omnivores, because they eat both animal food such as mice and birds and plant food such as fruit and berries. This makes them very flexible when looking for food.
1734.m: Martens eat both animals and plants.

1735.q: What usually makes conifers different from broadleaf trees?
a: They often keep their needles in winter too
They only grow in the desert
1735.e: Conifers like spruces or firs have narrow, hard needles instead of broad leaves. That is why many conifers stay green in winter too.
1735.m: Conifers often stay green in winter.

1736.q: Which disease that also affects farm cattle can African buffalo pass on?
1736.e: Buffalo can carry the germs of foot-and-mouth disease without being seriously ill themselves. That is why some regions have fences and checks between wild animals and cattle.
1736.m: Buffalo can pass on cattle diseases.

1737.q: Roughly how old can bearded vultures get in breeding centres?
1737.e: In a protected place without dangers, bearded vultures can get especially old. In breeding centres, some birds have lived to over 40.
1737.m: In breeding centres they get very old.

1738.q: What is the praying mantis's egg case called?
1738.e: The female produces a foam that hardens in the air. Many eggs lie safely inside it.

1739.q: What does the kingfisher use to dig its nest burrow?
a: it uses other animals' abandoned burrows
1739.e: The kingfisher loosens the soil with its beak and then shovels it out with its feet. Digging can take several days.
1739.m: The beak loosens, the feet shovel.

1740.q: What does a sparrow mainly eat in winter, when there are fewer insects?
1740.e: In winter there are hardly any insects, so the sparrow mainly eats seeds and grain. Bird feeders help it find enough even in the cold.

1741.q: What are birds called when some of them migrate and some stay?
1741.e: The robin is a so-called partial migrant. This means only some of the birds fly away in winter.
1741.m: Not all partial migrants fly away.

1742.q: Why is a box with wheels easier to push than one without wheels?
a: Because it makes the box lighter
Because wheels make the box float
1742.e: Wheels roll instead of sliding, so there is much less friction with the ground. That is why the box is easier to move.

1743.q: Where does the European pond turtle usually eat?
1743.e: The turtle swallows its food best under water. On land it finds this difficult.

1744.q: When can you see especially many red kites passing through Switzerland?
a: in autumn, when birds from the north pass through
in the middle of summer in great heat
only on one single day a year
1744.e: In autumn, red kites from more northern countries pass through Switzerland as well as the Swiss breeding birds. Then you can see many birds at once at good viewing spots.
1744.m: Many red kites pass through in autumn.

1745.q: What is the adult male wild boar called?
1745.e: The adult male wild boar is called a boar. It has large tusks in its mouth.
1745.m: The male wild boar is called a boar.

1746.q: What can you give a tired bumblebee on the ground?
a: Some sugar water so it gets its strength back
1746.e: You can carefully help an exhausted bumblebee with some sugar water on a spoon. This gives it new energy so it can fly on.

1747.q: Roughly how long does it take for blackbird eggs to hatch?
1747.e: After about two weeks of sitting on the eggs, the young blackbirds hatch. Before that, the female sits in the nest almost all the time.
1747.m: Blackbird eggs take about two weeks.

1748.q: What do you call a weather vane in the shape of a cockerel on a church tower?
1748.e: A weathercock is a metal figure on a church tower that turns in the wind. It shows which direction the wind is blowing from.
1748.m: The weathercock shows the wind direction.

1749.q: Which animal often leads a herd of wild horses?
1749.e: In many wild horse herds, an experienced lead mare takes charge. She knows good grazing places and watering holes.
1749.m: A lead mare often leads the herd.

1750.q: What is the female roe deer called?
1750.e: The female roe deer is called a doe. She has no antlers.
1750.m: The female roe deer is a doe.

1751.q: What does a pig do when something frightens it?
a: It squeals loudly and runs away
It stands completely still and stays silent
1751.e: When frightened or in danger, pigs often react by squealing loudly and running away fast. This also warns the other pigs in the group.

1752.q: Which large order of birds does the robin belong to?
1752.e: The robin belongs to the perching birds, a large group of mostly small songbirds. Sparrows and blackbirds belong to it too.

1753.q: Do bumblebees make as much honey as honeybees?
a: No, only very little for their own needs
They make no honey at all
They make more honey than bees
1753.e: Bumblebees only store small amounts of honey, enough for their own family. Honeybees, on the other hand, collect much more for the whole winter.
1753.m: Bumblebees make only a little honey.

1754.q: Roughly how long does a honeybee worker live in summer?
1754.e: In summer, the bees work very hard and so only live a few weeks. In winter, however, bees can live much longer.
1754.m: Summer bees live only a few weeks.

1755.q: Which group of animals does the mole eat most often?
1755.e: The mole specialises in small animals that live in the soil. Earthworms and insect larvae are what it eats most often.
1755.m: Worms and larvae are its main food.

1756.q: What happens to lake trout eggs in the gravel?
a: They develop there for weeks in the cold water
They hatch after just one hour
The parents guard them and keep them warm
1756.e: In the cold water, the embryos develop slowly inside the eggs. Only after weeks do the young fish hatch.
1756.m: Eggs develop slowly in cold gravel.

1757.q: What do newly hatched praying mantises eat?
a: Very small insects such as aphids or fruit flies
1757.e: The tiny creatures can only cope with small prey. They often eat their brothers and sisters too when it gets crowded.

1758.q: Which ape swings especially skilfully from branch to branch using its arms?
1758.e: Gibbons have very long arms and swing their way through the treetops. They can cross large gaps. Gorillas and baboons mostly move on the ground.
1758.m: Gibbons swing from branch to branch.

1759.q: Why do earthworms usually dig their tunnels straight down?
a: So they quickly reach deeper, damper layers of soil
So they find gold in the ground
So they meet other kinds of animals
1759.e: Deeper in the ground it stays damper and warmer than at the surface. Vertical tunnels get the worm there quickly.
1759.m: Vertical tunnels lead to damp soil.

1760.q: How does a tiger hunt its prey?
a: It creeps up quietly and surprises it
It just waits in its cave
1760.e: Tigers creep up silently on their prey and then suddenly attack. This method is called stalking.

1761.q: Roughly how long does it take for the turtle eggs to hatch?
1761.e: The eggs lie buried in the warm sand for about two months before the little turtles hatch. Then they dig their way up together.
1761.m: The eggs hatch after about two months.

1762.q: What does the German saying “as cheeky as a sparrow” mean?
1762.e: Because sparrows often boldly peck up crumbs right at people's feet, Germans say “as cheeky as a sparrow”. The saying describes someone who behaves boldly.
1762.m: The sparrow stands for cheeky and bold.

1763.q: What do newly hatched whitefish larvae live on at first?
1763.e: The yolk sac hangs from the larva's body and contains nutrients. Only when it is used up do the young fish look for food themselves.
1763.m: The yolk sac feeds the larvae first.

1764.q: What do you call animals like the hamster that eat both seeds and small insects?
1764.e: Hamsters eat plant foods such as grain and now and then small insects as well. Animals like this are called omnivores.

1765.q: How often should fresh water be available for guinea pigs?
a: It is not needed at all
1765.e: Guinea pigs should have clean, fresh water at all times. Without enough water they can quickly become ill.

1766.q: When are reindeer calves usually born?
1766.e: The calves are born after a pregnancy of about seven and a half months. Then there will soon be fresh food.

1767.q: What does it show when several grey herons nest together in one tree?
a: They are forming a colony, which is typical for them
This never happens with grey herons
It means they are usually ill
They fight until only one is left
1767.e: Nesting together in colonies is normal, typical breeding behaviour for the grey heron. Several nests can be in one tree at the same time.
1767.m: Colony nesting is normal for grey herons.

1768.q: What do budgies need to keep their beaks busy?
1768.e: Budgies like nibbling twigs or special toys. This keeps them busy and wears down the beak.

1769.q: What shape are the little cells in a wasps' nest usually?
1769.e: The combs in the nest are made of many six-sided cells. Each cell holds an egg or a larva.

1770.q: Which wild bird is the farm duck descended from?
1770.e: Most farm ducks were bred from the wild mallard a long time ago. You can also see mallards on many Swiss lakes.
1770.m: Farm ducks come from the mallard.

1771.q: What colours does an orca typically have?
1771.e: The orca has a striking black and white pattern. This makes it easy to recognise in the water.

1772.q: What are the bristles on a pig's skin made of?
1772.e: Bristles are the typical, rather hard hairs on a pig's skin. In the past they were even used to make brushes.
1772.m: Bristles are a pig's stiff hairs.

1773.q: Grasshoppers develop without a pupa stage. What is this kind of development in insects called?
1773.e: In incomplete metamorphosis there is an egg, a larva and an adult, but no pupa. Butterflies, on the other hand, go through complete metamorphosis with a pupa.
1773.m: Development without a pupa is called incomplete metamorphosis.

1774.q: What happens when you look into a jet of water from a garden hose in the sunshine?
a: You can see a small rainbow
1774.e: Sunlight is bent and split up in the tiny water droplets. This produces the colours, similar to a real rainbow.
1774.m: Water droplets and sunlight make colours.

1775.q: Which big cat is one of the enemies of the lowland tapir?
1775.e: In South America, the jaguar hunts young and adult tapirs. Pumas can also catch young ones.
1775.m: The jaguar hunts tapirs in South America.

1776.q: How does the golden eagle often use rising air when flying?
a: It glides for a long time on thermals without flapping
It always flies close to the ground
It always stays sitting near the ground
1776.e: Golden eagles use rising warm air, called thermals, to circle over the mountains for a long time while saving energy. This lets them search large areas for prey.

1777.q: Who feeds young cuckoos in the nest?
1777.e: The cuckoo lays its egg in the nest of small birds, for example the reed warbler. These other birds then feed the cuckoo chick.

1778.q: What is the biggest danger for ring-tailed lemurs?
a: Losing their habitat through logging and burning of forests
A lack of insects in the sea
1778.e: In Madagascar, many forests are being cleared. This means ring-tailed lemurs lose food and places to sleep.

1779.q: What happens to most adult garden spiders in winter?
a: They die, only the eggs survive
They sleep deep in a cave
1779.e: When it gets cold, most adult garden spiders die. Only the well-protected eggs in the cocoon survive the winter.

1780.q: Which body parts do all beetles, including dung beetles, have to protect their wings?
1780.e: The hard wing cases lie like a shield over the delicate flying wings. To fly, the beetle opens them out to the sides.
1780.m: Wing cases protect the flying wings.

1781.q: What is different about wild dog packs compared with many other animals?
a: The females often leave the pack
1781.e: In wild dogs it is usually the females that leave and look for a new pack. The males more often stay in the pack they were born in.
1781.m: Wild dog females often move away.

1782.q: Which animal has a long trunk and huge ears?
1782.e: The elephant is the largest land animal and uses its trunk to grab, drink and smell. Elephants live in Africa and Asia.

1783.q: Roughly how long does a hedgehog hibernate?
1783.e: From autumn to spring, the hedgehog sleeps for several months almost without a break. It only wakes up when it gets warm again.

1784.q: How do lions move about when they are not hunting?
a: They walk in a relaxed way and save energy
They always run at top speed
1784.e: Because hunting takes a lot of energy, lions usually move slowly and sparingly in everyday life. Only to attack do they suddenly speed up.

1785.q: How long do young otters usually stay with their mother?
1785.e: Young otters stay with their mother for about a year, until they can hunt and survive on their own. After that, they look for their own territory.
1785.m: The young stay about a year with their mother.

1786.q: Which muscle separates the chest from the belly and is important for breathing?
1786.e: The diaphragm tightens when you breathe in and makes the chest bigger. This makes air flow into the lungs.

1787.q: What is special about a reindeer's hair?
1787.e: Many of the hairs are filled with air inside. This keeps the warmth close to the body.

1788.q: What role does the cuckoo play with pests in the forest?
a: It has nothing to do with them
1788.e: Because the cuckoo also likes eating poisonous and hairy caterpillars that other birds avoid, it helps the forest keep pests under control. This makes it useful for trees and plants.
1788.m: The cuckoo eats many harmful caterpillars.

1789.q: The scientific name of the puma is Puma concolor. What does “concolor” mean?
1789.e: Concolor means of one colour. The name suits the coat of adult pumas, which has neither spots nor stripes.

1790.q: What do you call a group of wolves that lives and hunts together?
1790.e: A wolf pack is usually a family of parents and their young from several years. Together they hunt, play and defend their territory.
1790.m: Wolves usually live in family packs.

1791.q: What is the perch called in Ticino?
1791.e: In Italian, the perch is called pesce persico. Luccio is the pike and trota the trout.
1791.m: In Ticino, the perch is called “pesce persico”.

1792.q: How does a seahorse move compared with other fish?
a: It is one of the slowest fish of all
It is the fastest fish in the sea
1792.e: Seahorses are among the slowest swimmers of all fish. That is why they prefer to hold on with their tails rather than swim freely.
1792.m: Seahorses are among the slowest fish.

1793.q: Roughly how fast can a lion run over a short distance?
1793.e: Lions can sprint very fast for a short time to catch prey. Over longer distances, though, they tire quickly.
1793.m: Lions sprint fast for a short time.

1794.q: Apart from the Alps, in which other mountain ranges of the world does the bearded vulture live?
a: For example in the Himalayas and in Ethiopia
1794.e: The bearded vulture is found not only in the Alps but also in other mountains such as the Himalayas, the Caucasus or the mountains of Ethiopia. Everywhere it prefers steep, rocky landscapes.
1794.m: Bearded vultures live in many mountain ranges worldwide.

1795.q: How does the common buzzard typically hold its wings when circling?
a: Slightly raised in a shallow V shape
1795.e: When circling, the common buzzard often holds its broad wings raised in a shallow V shape. This makes its flight outline quite typical and easy to recognise.

1796.q: What do wild boar especially like to eat in the forest?
1796.e: Wild boar root up the forest floor with their snouts and find acorns, roots, insects and worms. So they eat almost anything they find in the ground.
1796.m: Wild boar root for acorns and worms.

1798.q: What is the largest Pacific salmon called?
1798.e: The king salmon, or Chinook, grows especially large. It can be over a metre long.
1798.m: The king salmon is the largest Pacific salmon.

1799.q: Why do some alpine sheep in Switzerland wear a bell around their neck?
a: So that they are easier to find and you can hear where they are
So that they can smell better
So that they can run faster
So that they don't get cold
1799.e: A bell around the neck helps the shepherd hear the sheep even from far away and find them more easily. So they don't get lost so easily in the mountains.

1800.q: What do penguins do when their partner comes back after breeding?
a: They recognise each other by their voices
They recognise each other by smell
They no longer recognise each other at all
1800.e: In a huge colony, all penguins sound similar, but each one has its own voice. This is how partners find each other and parents find their chicks.
1800.m: Penguins recognise each other by voice.

1801.q: What is a baby chicken called?
1801.e: A chick hatches from an egg. It is fluffy and very small.

1802.q: What causes the tides on the coasts of the seas?
a: The pull of the moon and the sun
1802.e: The moon’s gravity pulls slightly on the sea water, which makes bulges of water. The sun also adds to this effect.
1802.m: Tides are caused by the pull of the moon.

1803.q: How does the barn swallow usually breed, alone or with others?
a: Always strictly alone with no other swallows nearby
Only together with bats in the same nest
1803.e: Barn swallows often breed in loose small colonies, for example several nests in one barn. Sometimes, though, they also breed alone.

1804.q: Which fur colours can a brown bear have despite its name?
a: From light brown to dark brown to almost black
1804.e: Despite its name, a brown bear's fur can vary a lot in colour, from light brown to almost black. The exact colour often depends on the region where the bear lives.
1804.m: Brown bear fur varies a lot in colour.

1805.q: How does the kingfisher usually fly?
a: fast, straight and low over the water
only gliding high in the sky
1805.e: The kingfisher flies very fast, in a straight line and close to the water's surface. This way of flying helps it get quickly from one perch to the next.
1805.m: Fast, straight, low flight over water.

1806.q: What is special about the dorsal fin of male orcas?
a: It is very tall and can measure up to 1.8 metres
1806.e: Male orcas have a tall, straight dorsal fin. In females it is smaller and slightly curved.
1806.m: Male orcas have a tall dorsal fin.

1807.q: Which animal family does the lion belong to?
1807.e: The lion belongs to the cat family, just like the tiger and the pet cat. It is one of the biggest big cats in the world.
1807.m: The lion is a big cat.

1808.q: What happens to the fur of some least weasels in winter?
1808.e: Especially in colder, snowy areas, some least weasels change their fur to white. In milder regions, such as large parts of Switzerland, the fur often stays brown.

1809.q: Where does the German name “Siebenschläfer” (seven sleeper) for the edible dormouse come from?
a: From its hibernation of about seven months
Because its fur has seven colours
Because it wakes up seven times a night
1809.e: The edible dormouse hibernates for an especially long time, about seven months. That is how it got this name.
1809.m: The name comes from its long hibernation.

1810.q: What do slow-worms often do first in spring after their winter rest?
1810.e: After the cold, they first have to warm up. To do this, they lie in sunny, sheltered spots.

1811.q: Which wild goose is our farm goose descended from?
1811.e: Most farm geese were bred from the greylag goose a long time ago. The greylag goose can still be found here as a wild bird today.
1811.m: The farm goose comes from the greylag goose.

1812.q: What does the tiger shark, which is not very fussy, eat?
1812.e: The tiger shark eats fish, turtles and sometimes even rubbish that it mistakes for prey. It is thought to be one of the least fussy eaters in the sea.
1812.m: The tiger shark eats almost anything.

1813.q: What material do sparrows sometimes pinch from people for their nests?
1813.e: Sparrows like building their nests from soft materials and sometimes use threads, wool or paper that they find. This makes the inside of the nest nice and soft.
1813.m: Sparrows also use wool and threads.

1814.q: How does a female edible frog typically lay her eggs?
a: In lumpy clumps of spawn in the water
One at a time, hidden on land
In a nest she builds from twigs
1814.e: The eggs are laid in the water in large, jelly-like clumps of spawn. These clumps often stick to water plants.
1814.m: Eggs are laid in clumps of spawn.

1815.q: What does a cockerel do when danger threatens?
a: It warns the hens with a call
It runs away on its own
1815.e: A cockerel protects its hens and warns them with loud calls when an enemy comes near. This gives the hens time to escape.

1816.q: Roughly how many eggs does a Roman snail usually lay in one clutch?
1816.e: In each clutch, a Roman snail lays about 40 to 60 eggs. The clutch lies well hidden in the soil.
1816.m: A clutch has many small eggs.

1817.q: How many toes does a guinea pig have on its front feet?
1817.e: Guinea pigs have four toes on their front feet but only three on their back feet. You can see this well if you look closely.
1817.m: Guinea pigs have four toes at the front.

1818.q: What is behind the horns of a male chamois and gets bigger during the rut?
1818.e: Behind the male's horns there is a scent gland that grows much bigger during the rut. With its scent he marks his territory and attracts females.
1818.m: The scent gland grows during the rut.

a: In the south of the Earth, where it is cool
1819.e: Most penguins live on cool coasts in the south of the Earth, for example in Antarctica. There are no wild penguins at the North Pole.
1819.m: Penguins live almost only in the south of the Earth.

1821.q: How is a dung beetle different from a fly that lives in dung?
a: The beetle has hard wing cases, the fly only two wings
The beetle has eight legs, the fly six
The fly has a shell, the beetle doesn't
1821.e: Flies have only one pair of wings, while beetles have wing cases and flying wings. But both are insects with six legs.
1821.m: Beetles have wing cases, flies don't.

1822.e: Feathers keep the chicken warm and protect it from rain. They are very light.

1823.q: What does a trout egg need for a fish to develop from it?
a: Cool water with lots of oxygen
1823.e: Trout eggs lie in the gravel, where cool water rich in oxygen flows through. Only then can the little fish develop inside the egg.

1824.q: What is a koi compared with a goldfish?
a: A different, usually bigger relative of the goldfish
1824.e: The koi is also a member of the carp family and related to the goldfish, but it is a different species and usually grows bigger. Koi are often kept in large ponds.

1825.q: Where does the great spotted woodpecker build its nest?
a: in a hole it pecks out of a tree itself
in a grass nest on the ground
in a crack in a rock
1825.e: With its strong beak, it pecks a hole in a tree trunk. Later the female lays her eggs in it.
1825.m: It pecks out its own hole.

1826.q: What colour are a blackbird's legs usually?
1826.e: The blackbird's legs are usually dark, almost blackish. This goes well with the rest of the male's feathers.

1827.q: In the common swift, all four toes point forwards. What are these feet good for?
1827.e: With its short feet and sharp claws, the swift holds on to vertical walls. They are hardly any use for walking.
1827.m: Swift feet are made for clinging.

1828.q: What kind of animal is a hamster first and foremost?
1828.e: The hamster belongs to the group of rodents, just like mice and rats. Rodents have special teeth for gnawing.

1829.q: What danger do people pose to the African wild dog?
1829.e: Its habitat is getting smaller and broken up by settlements and farming. This makes life hard for the packs.

1830.q: What is a golden eagle's nest mainly made of?
1830.e: The nest is built from branches and twigs and lined with soft material. Used for many years, it can become very large and heavy.

1831.q: How does an alpine marmot usually move about when it is not fleeing?
a: It walks slowly on four legs
It mainly hops like a kangaroo
It glides through the air like a bird
