1831.e: In everyday life, the marmot moves rather slowly and carefully on four legs. But when there is danger, it can run very fast to its burrow.
1831.m: It normally walks slowly on four legs.

1832.q: What are donkeys sometimes used for in the Swiss mountains?
1832.e: On hikes in the Alps, donkeys often carry the hikers' luggage. They are sure-footed on stony paths.

1833.q: Roughly how often does a mother rhino have a new baby?
a: Only once in her whole life
1833.e: A mother rhino only has a new calf every two to five years. This is because pregnancy lasts so long.

1834.q: How heavy can a fully grown bison bull get?
1834.e: American bison bulls often weigh up to about 1,000 kilograms. This makes them some of the heaviest land animals in North America.
1834.m: Bison bulls weigh about a tonne.

1835.q: Do female African elephants have tusks too?
a: Yes, usually both males and females have tusks
1835.e: Unlike some other kinds of elephant, in the African elephant both females and males usually have tusks. They keep growing throughout life.

1836.q: How many toes does a stone marten have on each paw?
1836.e: Like many carnivores, the stone marten has five toes on each paw, each with a sharp claw. This helps it climb and dig.
1836.m: Five toes per paw on a stone marten.

1837.q: After metamorphosis, how long do young alpine newts take until they are old enough to breed?
1837.e: After their transformation, young alpine newts first live on land for a few years. Only after about two to three years are they mature and able to breed themselves.
1837.m: They are mature after a few years.

1838.q: Which animal belongs to the deer family, like the red deer?
1838.e: The roe deer belongs to the deer family, like the red deer. But the red deer is much bigger than the roe deer.
1838.m: Roe deer and red deer are related.

1839.q: Roughly how fast does light travel?
1839.e: The speed of light in a vacuum is almost 300,000 kilometres per second. It is seen as the absolute speed limit in the universe.
1839.m: Light travels about 300,000 km every second.

1840.q: Roughly how heavy is a carrion crow?
1840.e: An adult carrion crow weighs about 400 to 600 grams. The weight can vary a little with the season.
1840.m: A carrion crow weighs about half a kilogram.

1841.q: What are the fine lines that run like a net through a butterfly's wings called?
1841.e: The wing veins support the thin wing, a bit like the struts of an umbrella. Body fluid also flows through them.

1842.q: What does it sound like when lots of sparrows chirp together in a hedge?
1842.e: When lots of sparrows sit together, it can sound quite loud and lively. All this chirping is also called sparrow chatter.
1842.m: Lots of sparrows make loud chatter.

1843.q: Can a puma roar like a lion?
a: No, it hisses, spits and purrs
Yes, just as loudly as a lion
1843.e: Pumas belong to the small cats and cannot really roar. They purr, hiss and give shrill screams.

1844.q: Roughly how long does the metamorphosis from larva to land animal take?
1844.e: From the newly hatched larva to the young animal living on land, about two to four months pass, depending on conditions. After that, the young newts leave the water.

1845.q: Can young pandas climb trees early on?
1845.e: Pandas practise climbing even as small cubs. This way they can get to safety from danger.

1846.q: How many pairs of legs does an adult woodlouse have?
1846.e: Woodlice have seven pairs of legs, so fourteen legs. Insects, on the other hand, have only three pairs of legs.
1846.m: Woodlice have seven pairs of legs.

1847.q: Where does the wels catfish like to be during floods?
a: In flooded areas along the banks
1847.e: During floods, wels catfish like to move into flooded areas where they find food. Afterwards, they go back into the river or lake.
1847.m: Floods open new hunting grounds for the wels.

1848.q: Does the blue whale mainly eat large fish?
a: No, it eats tiny crustaceans called krill
1848.e: Although the blue whale is huge, it only eats tiny crustaceans called krill. But it needs a great many of them.
1848.m: The biggest eater eats tiny animals.

1849.q: What decides how many eggs a female eagle owl lays in a year?
a: How much food there is at that time
Only the age of the male
Only the phase of the moon
Only the colour of the feathers
1849.e: The amount of food available affects how many eggs a female eagle owl lays. In years with lots of prey, there can be more eggs than in lean years.
1849.m: Food supply decides the eagle owl's egg count.

1850.q: How many antennae does a grasshopper have on its head?
1850.e: With its two antennae, the grasshopper feels and smells its surroundings. The antennae are very important for it.

1851.q: How long does an adult brown trout usually grow?
1851.e: Most brown trout grow 20 to 40 centimetres long. In very good waters, some can grow much bigger.
1851.m: It usually grows 20 to 40 cm long.

1852.q: How can you help woodlice in the garden on purpose?
a: With piles of leaves, dead wood and stones
1852.e: Woodlice need hiding places and food. Leaves, wood and stones provide both.
1852.m: Leaves and dead wood help woodlice.

1853.q: What is typical of barn swallows when it comes to their nesting place?
a: They often return to the same nest
They build on a new continent every year
They never nest in the same place twice
They share their nest with bats
1853.e: Many barn swallows are loyal to their breeding place and often fly back to the same barn after the winter. There they repair their old nest.
1853.m: It often returns to its old nest.

1855.q: What does the mole use to dig its tunnels?
1855.e: The mole's front paws are broad and strong like little shovels. It uses them to push the soil aside.

1856.q: What is a fat ball that you can hang up for great tits?
a: A food ball made of fat and seeds
1856.e: A fat ball is made of fat with seeds and grain mixed in. In winter it gives the birds lots of energy.

1857.q: How good is a pig's sense of smell?
a: Very good, much better than ours
Exactly the same as a human's
1857.e: Pigs have an excellent sense of smell, which lets them find food deep in the ground. That is why some pigs are even used to search for truffles.
1857.m: Pigs have a very fine sense of smell.

1858.q: What especially helps the edible dormouse climb trees?
a: its gliding skin between the legs
its suction pads on its paws
1858.e: The flexible toes with small claws give the edible dormouse a good grip when climbing. So it can move nimbly between branches.

1860.q: Which well-known natural product is made from honeydew?
1860.e: Bees collect honeydew from plant lice and turn it into forest honey. It is often darker than flower honey.
1860.m: Bees make forest honey from honeydew.

1861.q: Which well-known predatory fish is closely related to the perch?
1861.e: Like the perch, the zander belongs to the true perches. Pike, trout and carp belong to other families.
1861.m: The zander is a relative of the perch.

1862.q: What is the main reason why people often hunted or killed wild dogs?
a: They were seen as a danger to farm animals
Because of their teeth as jewellery
1862.e: Many farmers saw them as a threat to livestock and hunted them down. This contributed to their sharp decline.

1863.q: What do gorillas often do when they get a sudden fright?
1863.e: When a gorilla gets a fright, it may scream loudly or run away fast. Sometimes it also makes a threatening display to defend itself.

1864.q: How is the octopus different from the squid?
a: Only the squid has two extra long tentacles
The octopus has ten arms, the squid eight
Only the squid can squirt ink
1864.e: As well as eight arms, a squid has two longer tentacles. The octopus has only eight arms.

1865.q: Which group of animals does the koala belong to?
1865.e: The koala is a marsupial. These animals carry their young in a pouch on the mother's belly.

1866.q: What does forced labour in a prison camp (Gulag) mean?
a: Prisoners had to work unpaid in harsh conditions.
1866.e: In the Soviet Union millions of people had to do forced labour in camps called Gulags. Many died from cold, hunger and hard work.
1866.m: The Gulags forced people into hard labour.

1867.q: What is a group of elephants called?
1867.e: Elephants live together in a herd. This herd is usually made up of related female elephants and their young.

1868.q: Which butterfly has a pattern that looks like eyes?
1868.e: The peacock butterfly has four large eyespots on its wings. They look like the eyes of a big animal.

1869.q: Which animal can be dangerous to the barn owl?
a: A larger bird of prey such as the common buzzard
1869.e: Larger birds of prey or martens can be dangerous to the barn owl and its young. That is why it hides well during the day.
1869.m: Larger birds of prey are enemies.

a: A knock briefly disrupts the brain
A bone inside the brain breaks
1870.e: A hard knock can briefly move the brain inside the skull and disrupt how it works. Symptoms include, for example, headaches or dizziness.
1870.m: A knock can disrupt the brain.

1872.q: What does a butterfly usually do when it feels threatened?
1872.e: Butterflies cannot bite or sting. Their best escape is to flee: with quick wingbeats, they fly away.

1873.q: What is different about a cheetah's claws compared with most other cats?
a: It can hardly pull them in
It has no claws at all
It only has claws on its back legs
1873.e: A cheetah's claws almost always stay out. They grip the ground like spikes and help it run fast.

1874.q: What happens to the koala's habitat when forests are cleared?
a: It gets smaller and the koala finds less food
The koala simply moves to the sea
1874.e: When forests are cut down, the eucalyptus trees that the koala needs to live disappear. This makes it harder and harder for it to find enough food and safe trees.

1875.q: What happens to most adult grasshoppers when autumn and winter come?
a: They die before it gets really cold
1875.e: The adults usually don't survive the cold temperatures. But their eggs wait safely in the ground for spring.
1875.m: Usually only the eggs survive the cold.

1876.q: What are the special eyes of the housefly called?
1876.e: Compound eyes are made up of lots of tiny single eyes. This lets the fly see in almost all directions at once.

1877.q: What can people build for hedgehogs in the garden?
a: A hedgehog house as a shelter
A high fence with no gaps
1877.e: A small hedgehog house made of wood and leaves gives the hedgehog a safe shelter. It can hide or spend the winter there.
1877.m: A hedgehog house gives safe shelter.

1878.q: How do barn swallows often bring their young lots of small insects at once?
a: They form them into a compact ball of food in their beak
They first bring all the insects back up
They only ever bring a single insect
They let the young fetch the food themselves
1878.e: While hunting, barn swallows collect several small insects and form them into a compact ball in their beak. This way they can feed their young efficiently in one flight.
1878.m: Several insects are formed into a ball.

1879.q: How many piglets does a wild sow usually have at once?
1879.e: A wild sow usually has four to six young at the same time. This is called a litter.
1879.m: A wild sow usually has several young.

1880.q: How heavy can a fully grown beaver get?
1880.e: A fully grown beaver usually weighs between 20 and 30 kilograms. This makes it the heaviest native rodent in Europe.

1881.q: Which animals from South America are related to camels?
1881.e: Camels, llamas and alpacas belong to the same family, the camelids. Llamas and alpacas live in the Andes.

1882.q: How many ants live in a large wood ant nest?
a: A huge number, often over a hundred thousand
1882.e: Often over a hundred thousand ants live in a large wood ant nest. They all work together for the colony.
1882.m: A nest holds a huge number of ants.

1883.q: What is one way the magpie looks after its feathers?
a: By bathing in dust or sand
1883.e: Like many birds, magpies use dust or sand baths to care for their feathers and get rid of parasites. This behaviour helps them stay healthy.

1884.q: What is a very small baby gorilla called?
1884.e: A small gorilla is called an infant or a baby, as with other mammals. It stays with its mother for a long time.
1884.m: A little gorilla is called an infant.

1885.q: In which habitat do tapirs feel most at home?
1885.e: Tapirs need thick vegetation and water. That is why they live in rainforests and swamps.

a: in a nest in a tree
in a lodge in the water
in a crack in the rock high in the mountains
1886.e: The badger digs a large system of tunnels with many passages and chambers. This is called a sett.

1887.q: Which animals are hyenas most closely related to?
1887.e: Hyenas belong to the cat-like carnivores, so mongooses and cats are more closely related to them than dogs. Despite looking like dogs, they are not dogs.
1887.m: Hyenas are cat-like carnivores, not dogs.

1888.q: Which group of animals do jackals belong to?
1888.e: Jackals give birth to live young and feed them with milk. This is typical of mammals.
1888.m: Jackals feed their young with milk.

1889.q: What do tadpoles breathe with at first?
1889.e: At first, young tadpoles breathe in the water with gills, like fish. Later they grow lungs, which they then use to breathe air.
1889.m: Tadpoles breathe with gills at first.

1890.q: What is a big danger for badgers today?
1890.e: Sadly, many badgers are hit by cars when crossing roads. That is why some places have special tunnels for them.

1891.q: How does the great spotted woodpecker defend its territory?
a: by singing loudly like a canary
1891.e: When another woodpecker comes into its territory, the great spotted woodpecker drums and threatens it. This is how it defends its home.

1892.q: What role does the alpine salamander play in the mountain ecosystem?
a: As a predator, it keeps small insect numbers in check
It pollinates flowers like a bee
It is the most important food for whales
1892.e: As an insect-eater, the alpine salamander helps keep the numbers of small invertebrates in balance. So it is a small but important part of the food web.
1892.m: It helps keep insects in balance.

1893.q: How do male common frogs attract females in spring?
1893.e: In the breeding season, male common frogs call with quiet, growling sounds. These calls are much quieter than those of some other frog species.
1893.m: Males attract females with quiet calls.

1894.q: What is special about a rabbit's upper lip?
a: It is split in the middle
It is hard like a beak
It is very wide like a duck's
1894.e: Rabbits have an upper lip that is divided in the middle. This lets them nibble grass especially close to the ground.
1894.m: A rabbit's lip is split in the middle.

1895.q: How do people often see the stone marten, even though it is also useful?
a: As a sacred animal in Switzerland
As a predator dangerous to people
1895.e: Because of the damage it does to cars and sheds, the stone marten is often seen as a problem animal. People easily forget that it also eats lots of mice and is therefore useful.
1895.m: Stone martens are often wrongly seen as pests.

1897.q: In which seasons are earthworms especially active because the soil is damp and mild?
a: Only in the middle of winter
Never, they are always equally active
1897.e: In spring and autumn, the soil is often damp but not too cold. These are ideal conditions for earthworms.

1898.q: Where are young wild rabbits born?
1898.e: The mother rabbit builds a soft nest of grass and fur in a burrow. The young are born there naked and blind.
1898.m: Rabbits are born in an underground nest.

1899.q: Why do lots of mallards often gather in one place in autumn?
a: Because together they find food and protect themselves better
Because they want to hibernate there like bears
Because they hide their eggs there
Because they want to sleep there for ever
1899.e: In bigger groups, mallards find food more easily and notice danger more quickly. That is why they often gather at good spots in autumn.

1902.q: Does a koala usually live alone or in large groups?
1902.e: Koalas are loners and usually live on their own in their own area of trees. Males and females only meet briefly in the breeding season.

1903.q: What colour are adult carrion crows' eyes usually?
1903.e: The eyes of adult carrion crows are usually dark brown. This dark colour fits in well with the rest of their black appearance.
1903.m: Carrion crows have dark brown eyes.

1904.q: How far can a large kangaroo jump in one leap?
1904.e: A strong kangaroo can hop almost nine metres in a single leap. That is as long as two cars one behind the other.

1905.q: How many wings does a butterfly have?
1905.e: A butterfly has two front wings and two back wings. Together that makes four wings.

1907.q: How does a pair of beavers usually behave towards each other?
a: Beavers usually live in fixed pairs with one partner
1907.e: Beavers usually form fixed pairs that stay together for several years or even their whole lives. Together they look after their lodge, territory and young.
1907.m: Beavers usually live in fixed pairs.

1908.q: What is the difference between the African buffalo and the Asian water buffalo?
a: The water buffalo lives in Africa
The African buffalo lives in Asia
1908.e: Both belong to the cattle family, but they are different species. The water buffalo originally comes from Asia.
1908.m: African buffalo and water buffalo are different.

1909.q: What danger does modern boat traffic pose for great crested grebes?
a: Waves and disturbance can destroy nests and endanger chicks
1909.e: Strong waves from boats can tip over floating nests. Constant disturbance also makes breeding harder.
1909.m: Boat traffic endangers nests and chicks.

1910.q: What happens to your money when it is in a savings account at the bank?
a: It is kept safe there and you can take it out again later
It then belongs to the bank
It is automatically spent for you
1910.e: In a savings account the money stays yours. The bank just keeps it safe. You can take it out again later.
1910.m: The bank keeps it, but you still own it.

1911.q: When is the Roman snail especially active?
a: In damp weather, for example after rain
Only in the middle of winter
1911.e: The Roman snail loves damp air and is especially active after rain. When it is dry, it prefers to hide.

1912.q: What are the small, often blue-shimmering butterflies that are common in Switzerland called?
1912.e: Blues are a large family of small butterflies. Many males shimmer bright blue on the upper side of their wings.

1913.q: What can you often see on the shell of an old Roman snail?
a: More whorls than on a young snail
Fewer whorls than on a young snail
1913.e: The older and bigger a snail gets, the more whorls its shell has. So you can roughly estimate its age.

1914.q: What happens if you stand still and a wasp lands on you?
a: It usually flies away again after a short time
It stays sitting there for ever
1914.e: A wasp often just checks briefly whether something smells interesting. If you stay calm, it usually soon flies on.
1914.m: Stay calm and the wasp flies on.

1915.q: What is the siamang's inflatable throat sac for?
a: It stores water for dry times
It works as a swimming aid
1915.e: The siamang blows up its throat sac when it calls. This makes the sounds louder so they carry far.
1915.m: The throat sac makes the siamang loud.

1916.q: What colour is the fur of the European wild rabbit usually?
1916.e: The wild rabbit's fur is usually greyish brown. This colour helps it hide well in meadows and fields.
1916.m: Wild rabbits are usually greyish brown.

1917.q: How can you recognise an Asian elephant compared with an African elephant?
a: By the stripes in its fur
1917.e: Asian elephants have much smaller ears than African elephants. Their scientific name is Elephas maximus.

1918.q: How do a mother duck and her ducklings communicate?
a: With different sounds that the ducklings follow
They don't talk to each other at all
1918.e: The mother makes different sounds to call or warn her ducklings. The ducklings recognise these calls and follow her straight away.
1918.m: Sounds keep mother and ducklings together.

1919.q: What does a butterfly do when it is too cold outside?
a: It looks for food in the snow
1919.e: Without enough warmth, the butterfly's flight muscles can't work properly. That is why it sits still when it is cold.
1919.m: It can't fly when it is cold.

1920.q: How do baboons often find water in dry areas?
a: They dig for water in dry riverbeds
They catch rain with their tails
1920.e: Baboons can dig holes in dry riverbeds and so reach groundwater. This helps them in dry seasons.

a: Karl Marx's close friend and co-author
1921.e: Friedrich Engels worked closely with Karl Marx. Together they wrote important texts about communism.
1921.m: Engels was Marx's closest fellow thinker.

1922.q: How does an earthworm move forward even though it has no legs?
a: It stretches and squeezes its body in turn
It pushes itself along with wings
1922.e: By squeezing and stretching its ring-shaped muscles, the earthworm pushes itself forward bit by bit. Its tiny bristles help it hold on.

1923.q: How does a roe buck show that an area belongs to him?
a: He rubs his antlers on small trees
He lays stones in a circle
He builds a nest of branches
1923.e: The roe buck rubs his antlers on young trees and bushes. In doing so he leaves his scent, so other bucks know the area is taken.
1923.m: The roe buck marks his area on young trees.

1924.q: Roughly how long does an adult slow-worm grow?
1924.e: Most slow-worms grow to 40 to 50 centimetres long. They don't usually get much longer.
1924.m: Slow-worms usually grow to about 50 centimetres.

1925.q: How does the okapi usually move about?
a: At a calm walk through the forest
1925.e: Okapis usually move slowly and quietly through the thick undergrowth. But when there is danger, they can flee quickly.
1925.m: Okapis move quietly through the forest.

1926.q: How can you tell individual giraffes apart?
a: By their unique pattern of patches
By the colour of their eyes
By the sound of their voice
By the size of their ears
1926.e: Every giraffe has its own pattern of patches, like a human fingerprint. No two giraffes look exactly the same.
1926.m: Every giraffe has its own patch pattern.

1927.q: At best, how old can a barn swallow get?
1927.e: Some ringed barn swallows have lived to about 8 years old. But that is much more than the average.
1927.m: The record age is about eight years.

1928.q: What is it called when other group members help to raise the young?
1928.e: Many animals in the group guard and feed the young. This is called a helper system or cooperative breeding.
1928.m: The whole group helps with the young.

1929.q: What danger does plastic rubbish in the sea pose for sea turtles?
a: They mistake plastic bags for jellyfish
Plastic makes the water too warm
1929.e: Floating plastic bags often look like jellyfish in the water. Turtles eat them by mistake, which can harm them badly.
1929.m: Plastic bags are mistaken for jellyfish.

1930.q: What role do railway embankments play for the common wall lizard in Switzerland?
a: They offer warm, stony habitats where it can spread
They are completely unsuitable for the wall lizard
1930.e: Railway embankments are stony, dry and sunny, which makes them ideal for the wall lizard. This has let the species spread further along railway lines.
1930.m: Railway embankments are good substitute habitats.

1931.q: What are lions often called because of their strength?
1931.e: Because of its size, strength and mane, the lion is often called the “king of the animals”. Yet it doesn't live in the jungle at all, but in the savannah.
1931.m: The lion is often called king of the animals.

1932.q: Which Swiss village is famous for its white storks?
1932.e: Altreu in the canton of Solothurn is famous for its stork colony. You can watch lots of storks nesting there.

1933.q: Why does a stone marten sometimes go into a warm car engine in winter?
a: Because the engine still gives off heat after a drive
Because it wants to drink petrol there
Because it wants to lay eggs there
Because it likes the engine noise
1933.e: A car that has just been driven has a warm engine compartment, which makes a cosy shelter for the stone marten. Unfortunately, this can lead to damage to hoses and cables.
1933.m: Warm engines attract stone martens in winter.

1934.q: What is typical of an alpine newt's tail in the water?
a: It is flattened at the sides like a rudder
It is round like a mouse's
1934.e: In the water, the tail, which is flattened at the sides, works like a paddle to push it along. This lets the alpine newt swim skilfully.
1934.m: The flat tail works like a paddle.

1935.q: What role does the brown bear play in many old European legends and stories?
a: It is often seen as a strong and mighty forest animal
It is usually shown as especially weak
It is shown as a pet on farms
It is often shown as a small cheeky insect
1935.e: In many old legends and stories from Europe, the brown bear stands for strength and power. In the past it was one of the biggest and most feared animals in the forests.
1935.m: The bear is seen as a strong forest animal.

1936.q: What happens to most of the wasps in a colony in autumn?
1936.e: When it gets cold, the wasps can no longer find food. Then almost all the wasps in a colony die, except the young queens.

1937.q: Who usually makes the laws in a dictatorship?
a: Only the dictator or a small group.
1937.e: In a dictatorship a single person or a small clique usually sets the rules. The people have no say in it.
1937.m: A dictator makes the laws alone.

1938.q: What can you see especially clearly on the throat of the pine marten's fur compared with the stone marten?
a: The pine marten's yellowish throat patch is usually not split
The pine marten has no throat patch at all
The stone marten has a blue throat patch
Both have identical red throat patches
1938.e: In the pine marten, the light, yellowish throat patch is usually one piece and not forked, unlike the often split white patch of the stone marten. This is an important feature for telling them apart.
1938.m: The pine marten has an unsplit throat patch.

1939.q: Which is the largest predator on land?
1939.e: The polar bear is one of the largest predators on land. Only some brown bears get about as heavy.
1939.m: The polar bear is a huge predator.

1940.q: What is the main reason Swiss glaciers are getting smaller and smaller?
1940.e: Because of rising temperatures, glaciers around the world lose ice every year. In the Swiss Alps this retreat is especially easy to measure.

1941.q: What colour is the fluffy down of a young mute swan?
1941.e: Young mute swans first have grey down. Only later do they turn white like their parents.
1941.m: Young swans are grey at first.

1942.q: What happens to many great crested grebes from northern Europe in winter?
a: They move to milder areas such as coasts or large lakes
They get stuck in the ice
1942.e: Because frozen lakes offer no food, many birds move to ice-free areas. These are often coastal regions or large, open lakes.
1942.m: In winter, many move to ice-free water.

1943.q: Roughly how heavy can a badger get?
1943.e: In autumn, when it has eaten a lot of fat, a badger can weigh up to 20 kilograms. In spring it is much lighter.

1944.q: Where does a baby ring-tailed lemur usually hold on in its first days of life?
a: In a nest on the ground
To a rock on its own
1944.e: At first the baby clings to its mother's belly. Later it rides on her back.
1944.m: Baby lemurs cling to their mother.

1945.q: How many toes does an edible frog have on each back foot?
1945.e: Like most frog species, the edible frog has five toes on each back foot. They are joined by webbing.
1945.m: Five webbed toes on each back foot.

1946.q: What is the elk of Europe and Asia called, as opposed to North America?
1946.e: The Eurasian elk lives in Europe and northern Asia. Other subspecies live in North America.
1946.m: There are elk in Eurasia and America.

1948.q: What does the African wild dog's head usually look like?
a: Its muzzle is pink and hairless
1948.e: The muzzle is usually black, and the head can also have yellowish-brown tones. The coat overall is short and patchy.

1952.q: Which time of day does the alpine salamander usually avoid when it is sunny and hot?
1952.e: In great heat and strong sun, the alpine salamander hides so that it doesn't dry out. It prefers cooler, damper conditions.
1952.m: It avoids heat when it can.

1953.q: Which mineral is especially important for strong bones and teeth?
1953.e: Calcium is an important building material for bones and teeth. Dairy products contain particularly a lot of it.
1953.m: Calcium makes bones and teeth strong.

1954.q: What is the Swiss law that sets the rules for dealing with wolves called?
1954.e: The Hunting Act sets out how the wolf is protected in Switzerland and under what conditions its numbers may be controlled. It is changed and debated again and again.
1954.m: The Hunting Act governs wolf protection.

1955.q: How do adult male Asian elephants usually live?
a: Alone or in small bachelor groups
In the water, with no contact with land
1955.e: The bulls leave the herd as young males. After that they often roam on their own.

1956.q: What is a dolphin's signature whistle?
a: Its own whistle, like a name
A song for going to sleep
A call only made when eating
1956.e: Every dolphin has its own whistle that it uses to identify itself to others. It is almost like having its own name.
1956.m: Every dolphin has its own whistle.

1958.q: Roughly how long does it take for a cuckoo chick to hatch from the egg?
1958.e: The cuckoo egg takes about two weeks until the chick hatches. It often hatches even a little sooner than the host birds' eggs.
1958.m: Cuckoo eggs take about two weeks.

1959.q: What should children do if they come across a fire salamander in the wild?
a: Watch it calmly without touching it or taking it away
Hold it in their bare hands for a long time
1959.e: Because the fire salamander can give off poison and is protected, you should only watch it from a distance. That keeps both the animal and people safe.

1960.q: In which habitat does the common buzzard feel especially at home?
a: At the edges of woods near open fields
1960.e: The common buzzard prefers a landscape with woodland edges, single trees and open meadows or fields. There it finds good perches and enough prey.
1960.m: It prefers woodland edges and open fields.

1961.q: What does a young queen bee do before she can lay eggs?
a: She goes on a mating flight with drones
She builds a new comb on her own
She eats only pollen for a week
1961.e: On the mating flight, the young queen mates in the air with several drones. After that she can lay eggs for years.
1961.m: The mating flight lets the queen lay eggs.

1962.q: What is an important difference between toads and frogs?
a: Toads have shorter back legs and tend to crawl
1962.e: Compared with frogs, toads have shorter back legs. That is why they crawl more instead of jumping far.
1962.m: Toads have shorter legs than frogs.

1963.q: What was the name of a well-known border crossing between East and West Berlin?
1963.e: Checkpoint Charlie was the most important border crossing for foreigners between East and West Berlin. Today it is a well-known tourist spot.
1963.m: Checkpoint Charlie was a border crossing in Berlin.

1964.q: Why do ducks often waddle so funnily from side to side when they walk on land?
a: Because their legs are set far back on their body
Because they are too heavy to walk
Because they can only stand on one leg
Because they still have to learn to walk
1964.e: A duck's legs are set further back on its body, which is good for swimming. When walking on land, this leads to a waddling walk.
1964.m: Duck legs are set far back.

1965.q: What does the queen wasp build first in spring, before the colony grows?
a: A long tunnel in the ground
1965.e: The queen starts with a few small combs made of paper. She lays her first eggs in them.

1966.q: From which neighbouring country did the brown bears seen in the Swiss National Park come?
1966.e: The brown bears come from a group of bears in Trentino in northern Italy. From there, young bears sometimes wander as far as the Engadine.
1966.m: Bears in the Engadine come from Italy.

1967.q: Where in Switzerland is the wood mouse found?
a: Almost everywhere, in woods and in the countryside
Only high up on the highest peaks
1967.e: The wood mouse is widespread in Switzerland and lives in woods, fields and gardens.
1967.m: Wood mice live almost everywhere in Switzerland.

1968.q: Does the pike hunt more by day or by night?
a: Only in the middle of the night
Never, it doesn't hunt at all
1968.e: Pike mainly hunt by day, especially at dawn and dusk. That is when many prey fish are also active and on the move.
1968.m: The pike mainly hunts by day.

1969.q: Which mammal, a good swimmer and diver, also hunts brown trout?
1969.e: The otter mainly eats fish. Beavers, muskrats and coypus also swim well, but they eat plants.

1970.q: How long can an adult grass snake get in Switzerland?
1970.e: Females usually grow bigger than males. Some reach a good metre.

1971.q: What does a roe deer in the woods do when it notices a person?
a: It stands still, watches and then usually runs away fast
It walks straight towards the person
1971.e: Roe deer are very shy animals. Usually they first stand still and then run away quickly.
1971.m: Roe deer are shy and flee quickly.

1972.q: How many teeth does an adult cat normally have?
1972.e: An adult cat normally has 30 teeth, while a dog has 42. The sharp cutting teeth help it cut up meat.

1974.q: What is a feature of the grass snake's teeth?
a: It has many small teeth that curve backwards
It has big venom fangs at the front
It has no teeth at all
It has tusks like a wild boar
1974.e: The teeth hold on to slippery prey. They curve backwards.

1975.q: What does the perch mainly use to track down prey?
1975.e: The perch hunts by sight and sees its prey in clear water. Its lateral line also helps it.
1975.m: The perch hunts with its eyes.

1977.q: Why do you rarely see a badger, even though there are many in Switzerland?
a: because it is out and about at night
because it flies away in winter
because it only lives high in the mountains
1977.e: The badger sleeps during the day in its sett underground. Only when it gets dark does it go looking for food.
1977.m: The badger is out at night.

1978.q: What is the male chicken called?
1978.e: The male chicken is called a cockerel. It often has a bigger comb and more colourful feathers than the female.
1978.m: The cockerel is the male chicken.

1979.q: In a dictatorship, can you simply start a new party if you disagree?
a: Yes, and you get money for it.
1979.e: In a dictatorship there is often only one permitted party. New parties that think differently are banned or fought against.

1980.q: Which animal family does the tiger belong to?
1980.e: The tiger is a big cat and belongs to the cat family. It is related to lions and leopards.
1980.m: The tiger is a big cat.

1981.q: Which country is part of the area where the white-handed gibbon lives?
1981.e: The white-handed gibbon lives in Thailand, Malaysia and Sumatra, among other places. Its home is South-East Asia.
1981.m: White-handed gibbons live in South-East Asia.

1982.q: Is hunting alpine ibex in Switzerland completely banned today?
a: No, it is allowed under control, with fixed quotas
Yes, it is banned everywhere without any exceptions
No, anyone may shoot as many as they like at any time
Yes, because the species has already died out in Switzerland again
1982.e: Because their numbers have recovered well, hunting ibex in Switzerland is allowed under strict rules and with fixed quotas. This keeps the population under control without putting it at risk.

1983.q: What is typical of a brown bear's shoulders?
a: A noticeable hump of muscle for powerful digging
A small comb like a bird's
1983.e: Brown bears have a clearly visible hump of muscle on their shoulders. It gives the front legs the strength they need to dig and turn over soil.
1983.m: The shoulder hump gives bears strength.

1984.q: Do tigers also have striped skin under their fur?
a: Yes, the stripes go right down to the skin
No, the skin is completely white
No, the skin is completely black
No, only the fur has stripes
1984.e: A tiger's stripes are not just in its fur but can also be seen on the skin underneath. So every tiger has its very own pattern.
1984.m: The stripes go down to the skin.

1985.q: How does a praying mantis usually behave during the day?
a: It often sits still among plants, lying in wait
It flies around all the time
It always sleeps in the ground
1985.e: Sitting still saves energy and helps with camouflage and hunting. If something edible moves, it is ready in an instant.
1985.m: It lies in wait instead of rushing around.

1986.q: In which surroundings do chimpanzees especially like to live?
1986.e: Chimpanzees like living best in thick rainforests, where there are lots of trees and fruit. Some also live in more open savannah.

1987.e: Llama wool is made into yarn, blankets and clothes. It is usually coarser than alpaca wool.
1987.m: Llama wool is made into textiles.

1988.q: Which bird often spends the winter in Africa but breeds in Switzerland and builds big nests on roofs or poles?
1988.e: The white stork flies to Africa in autumn and comes back in spring to breed. Storks build big nests on roofs or poles.

1989.q: Did the brown bear once live in Switzerland too?
a: Yes, but it was wiped out at the start of the 20th century
No, it never lived in Switzerland
Yes, it is still very common there
No, it only lived in Germany
1989.e: The brown bear was once widespread in Switzerland too. Hunting wiped it out, and the last one was shot in 1904 in the Grisons. Today, single bears occasionally wander in from Italy.
1989.m: The brown bear was once at home in Switzerland.

1990.q: What does the mole use its short tail for?
a: To feel its way in the dark
1990.e: The mole's short tail is very sensitive. When it moves backwards, it uses it to feel its way.
1990.m: The tail helps when moving backwards.

1991.q: What is dried dromedary dung sometimes used for in the desert?
1991.e: Where wood is scarce, dry dung can be burned. It burns well because it is very fibrous.
1991.m: Dry dung is used as fuel.

1992.q: Anglers release young trout from a fish farm into streams. Why do they do this?
a: So that there are more fish in the stream again
So that the stream gets cleaner
So that the trout eat less
So that the fish farm becomes empty
1992.e: When there are too few fish in a stream, young fish from a farm are released. Experts call this stocking. It is better if the fish can breed in the stream on their own.
1992.m: Releasing young fish is called stocking.

1993.q: Why do zoos sometimes keep bonobos?
a: For conservation breeding and to protect the species
So they can do tricks in a circus
1993.e: Zoos have breeding programmes that are meant to help save the species. Visitors also learn more about these endangered animals.
1993.m: Zoos help with breeding and education.

1994.q: Roughly how many young does a female adder have?
1994.e: In each litter, usually anything from a few to about a dozen young are born. The young are already venomous.
1994.m: A litter is about a dozen young.

1995.q: In which habitats does the stone marten feel especially at home in Switzerland?
a: In villages and towns, barns and attics
Only deep in untouched primeval forest
Only in very high mountain regions above 3,000 metres
1995.e: The stone marten has adapted well to life in villages and towns. There it looks for shelter in barns, attics or under roofs.
1995.m: Stone martens like living near people.

1996.q: What is a typical prey animal of the puma in North America?
1996.e: Pumas mainly hunt hoofed animals such as deer. They also eat smaller animals such as hares.

1997.q: Where do the larvae of many dung beetles develop?
a: In underground brood chambers with a store of dung
In the water of a pond
1997.e: The parents bury dung in a tunnel in the ground. The larva finds its food there and is protected.
1997.m: The larvae grow underground next to stored dung.

1998.q: What often happens to young male lions when they are about two to three years old?
a: They have to leave the pride
They stay with their mother for ever
They have young of their own
1998.e: Growing male lions are driven out by the head of the pride so that there is no competition. After that, they roam for a while alone or with other young males.
1998.m: Young male lions have to leave the pride.

1999.q: What was the Polish trade union movement that fought against the communist government called?
1999.e: Solidarność was founded in 1980 in the Gdańsk shipyards and led by Lech Wałęsa. It played a major part in ending communism in Poland.
1999.m: Solidarność fought for freedom in Poland.

2000.q: In 2006 the bear “Bruno” wandered from Italy all the way to Germany. Why was he shot there?
a: He came too close to villages and people
He was supposed to go to a zoo
2000.e: Bruno kept coming near houses and killed sheep. Because he was seen as a danger to people, he was shot in Bavaria in 2006.
2000.m: Bruno came too close to people and was shot in 2006.

2001.q: Roughly how old does a golden hamster get?
2001.e: Golden hamsters live on average only two to three years. That is quite short compared with many other pets.
2001.m: Hamsters live only a few years.

2002.q: What does the cockerel do in the evening when it gets dark?
a: It goes into the henhouse with the hens
It stays alone in the field
2002.e: In the evening, cockerels and hens go together to a raised, sheltered place in the henhouse. There they spend the night safe from enemies.
2002.m: In the evening, the cockerel goes in with the hens.

2003.q: How does a young cuckoo know how a real cuckoo calls, even though it grows up with other birds?
a: It learns it from its foster parents
It learns it from other young birds in the nest
2003.e: The young cuckoo grows up with other birds, but it still knows by instinct how a cuckoo looks and calls. It is born with this behaviour.
2003.m: Cuckoo behaviour is inborn, not learned.

2004.q: Which is the largest lynx species in the world?
2004.e: The Eurasian lynx is much bigger than its relatives in America and Spain. It can also catch bigger prey such as roe deer.
2004.m: The Eurasian lynx is the giant.

2005.q: How does the size of a wild dog pack often affect its hunting success?
a: Bigger packs often hunt more successfully
2005.e: More animals can coordinate better when hunting and defend their prey better. That is why sticking together is important.
2005.m: Big packs are often more successful.

2006.q: Roughly how long is an adult barn swallow, including its tail?
2006.e: An adult barn swallow measures about 17 to 19 centimetres including its forked tail. The long tail makes up a large part of its length.

2007.q: What does a lion do with its claws when it is not hunting?
a: It hides them in its fur
2007.e: Just like pet cats, lions can pull in their claws so that they don't get in the way when walking. For hunting, they put them out again.
2007.m: Lions can pull in their claws.

2008.q: What does the male eagle owl mainly do during the breeding season?
a: It brings food to the female sitting on the eggs
It sits on the eggs together with the female
It leaves the territory for the whole breeding season
It builds a second nest during this time
2008.e: While the female sits on the eggs, the male does the hunting and brings her food. This lets the female keep the eggs warm almost all the time.
2008.m: The male eagle owl hunts for the female on the eggs.

2009.q: Which group of vertebrates does the salmon belong to?
2009.e: The salmon has a skeleton made of bone and breathes with gills. That makes it a bony fish.
2009.m: The salmon is a bony fish.

2010.q: How is the small red compost worm different from the big earthworm called the lobworm?
a: It is smaller and lives in compost
It is much bigger than the lobworm
It digs deeper tunnels than the lobworm
2010.e: The compost worm usually stays small and likes living in leaves and compost. The lobworm grows bigger and digs deep tunnels in the soil.
2010.m: Compost worms are small and red.

2011.q: Where does the word “leopard” originally come from?
2011.e: People used to believe the leopard was a mix of a lion and a pard. That is where the word comes from, from the Greek parts “leon” and “pardos”.

2012.q: Do all adult aphids have wings?
a: No, there are aphids with wings and without wings
No, none of them can ever fly
2012.e: Within one species there are often both forms. Winged aphids appear mainly when new plants need to be colonised.
2012.m: There are winged and wingless aphids.

2013.q: Can the snow leopard roar loudly like a lion?
a: Yes, even louder than a lion
2013.e: The snow leopard hisses, mews and growls, but it doesn't roar like other big cats. Its voice box is built differently.

2015.q: How does a mother duck sometimes defend herself against enemies when her ducklings are in danger?
a: She distracts the enemy and flutters away as if injured
She bites the enemy with sharp teeth
She hides and leaves the ducklings alone
She flies far away straight away
2015.e: Some mother ducks pretend to have an injured wing to lure enemies away from their ducklings. This draws the danger away from their young.

2016.q: What sound does a panda often make to communicate?
a: A loud roar like a lion
2016.e: Pandas make rather quiet, bleating sounds. They are not as loud as other big bears.

2017.q: On which continent is the wolf not originally found in the wild?
2017.e: The wolf is found in the northern half of the world, in Europe, Asia and North America. In Australia, however, there are no wild wolves.
2017.m: There are no wolves in Australia.

2018.q: Which small animals does the earwig like to eat?
2018.e: Earwigs eat aphids and other tiny garden pests. That is why they are seen as useful.

2019.q: Why do newly hatched butterflies first have to let their wings dry?
a: Because the wings are still soft and crumpled
Because they are wet from the rain
2019.e: Straight after hatching, the wings are small and crumpled. Only when fluid flows into them and they dry do they become big and firm enough to fly.

2020.q: Why should you leave frogspawn in the pond?
a: Because it turns into little frogs
Because it falls apart at once
2020.e: The eggs of the common frog develop in the clumps of spawn. The common frog is protected in Switzerland, so you leave the spawn in the pond.

2021.e: Depending on the kind of flower, honey is golden yellow to dark brown. It tastes sweet and people like spreading it on bread.
2021.m: Honey is usually golden yellow to brown.

2022.q: How many cantons must ask for a referendum against a federal law for it to take place?
2022.e: As well as 50,000 voters, eight cantons together can also call for a referendum against a federal law. This is called a cantonal referendum.
2022.m: Eight cantons can call for a referendum.

2023.q: Why does the cockerel crow so loudly in the morning?
a: It is telling other cockerels: this is my place
2023.e: By crowing, the cockerel shows other cockerels where its territory is. This is the place that belongs to it.

2024.q: How do many livestock farmers in the Alps react to the return of single brown bears?
a: Many worry about their grazing animals and call for protection measures
Nobody notices the bears coming back
Everyone wants to keep the bears as pets straight away
2024.e: When single brown bears move into alpine regions, many livestock farmers worry about the sheep and goats in their pastures. That is why measures to protect herds, such as fences or guard dogs, are often discussed.
2024.m: The bears' return causes debate among farmers.

2025.q: Are koalas found in the wild in Switzerland?
a: No, you can only see them in zoos here
Yes, many koalas live in the Alps
2025.e: There are no wild koalas in Switzerland, because their only home is Australia. Here you can at most admire them in some zoos.
2025.m: Wild koalas only live in Australia.

2026.q: How does freshly sheared sheep's wool usually feel, because it contains a natural fat?
2026.e: Sheep's wool naturally contains a fat called lanolin. It makes the wool water-repellent and feel a bit greasy before it is washed.

2027.q: What sense do whiskers, which the jaguar also has, help with?
a: They help it feel its surroundings
2027.e: The touch hairs on the face are very sensitive. They help it feel obstacles and prey, especially in the dark.

2028.q: Which sound does the female mallard usually make?
2028.e: The well-known loud quacking usually comes from the female. The males call more quietly and hoarsely.

2029.q: What does a bee need the baskets on its back legs for?
2029.e: The bee collects flower dust in the little baskets on its back legs. This is how it brings the pollen back to the hive.

2030.q: Where do mosquitoes especially like to hide during the day?
a: In the middle of open meadows
2030.e: During the day, mosquitoes often rest in the shade of bushes or in damp, cool spots. In the evening they become more active.
2030.m: Mosquitoes rest in the shade by day.

2031.q: Roughly how big does an adult budgie get?
2031.e: An adult budgie measures about 18 centimetres from its head to the tip of its tail. That makes it a fairly small parrot.

a: An election to fill a post that has become vacant during the term
A second round in every election
An election only for substitute candidates without a party
2032.e: If an elected person resigns or dies during the term, a by-election is usually held. This fills the empty seat.
2032.m: By-elections fill posts that have become vacant.

2033.q: When are mosquitoes usually especially active?
a: In the evening and at night
2033.e: Many mosquitoes like flying best at dusk or at night, when it is cooler and damper. During the day they often hide in shady places.
2033.m: Mosquitoes like flying in the evening and at night.

2034.q: Where does the name “alpine newt” probably come from?
a: Because it is also common in mountain regions
Because it only lives on the Matterhorn
Because it looks like a mountain
2034.e: The alpine newt owes its name to the fact that it is also found high up in the mountains. In fact, though, it often lives in the lowlands too.
2034.m: The name comes from where it lives in the mountains.

2035.q: What do young pond skaters look like?
a: Like small adults, but without wings
2035.e: The larvae already have six legs and walk on the water. They only get wings later, if at all.
2035.m: Larvae look like small adults without wings.

2036.q: In which season does the sparrow usually start building its nest?
2036.e: In spring, when it gets warmer, sparrows start building their nests. It is the best time to raise chicks.
2036.m: Sparrows build their nests in spring.

2037.q: Which animal is one of the natural enemies of young blue whales?
2037.e: Groups of killer whales sometimes hunt small or weakened blue whales. Otherwise, healthy adult blue whales have hardly any enemies.

2038.q: How do earthworms help leaves disappear faster in autumn?
a: They pull the leaves into the soil and eat them
They gather the leaves into a pile for birds
They just leave the leaves lying there
2038.e: Earthworms pull fallen leaves into their tunnels and slowly eat them there. Over time, this turns the leaves into new, fertile soil.
2038.m: Worms pull leaves into the soil.

2039.q: What does a lion do to mark its territory?
a: It sprays scent marks and roars
It draws signs in the sand
2039.e: Lions leave scent marks and roar loudly so that other lions know where their area begins. This sometimes helps them avoid a fight.
2039.m: Scent marks show a lion's territory.

2040.q: How big can an otter's territory along a river be?
2040.e: An otter's territory can stretch for several kilometres along a river. Males often claim bigger territories than females.
2040.m: Territories stretch for kilometres along the river.

2041.q: What does a seahorse mainly use to swim forward?
a: A small fin on its back
2041.e: A small fin on its back flutters back and forth very fast. This moves the seahorse slowly forward.
2041.m: The back fin drives it forward.

2042.q: Roughly how many eucalyptus leaves does a koala eat in a day?
2042.e: A koala eats several hundred grams of eucalyptus leaves every day. That doesn't sound like much, but for its body it is a lot.
2042.m: Koalas eat lots of leaves every day.

2043.q: Why are dams in rivers often a problem for trout?
a: Because the trout can no longer swim to their spawning grounds
Because dams make the water too clear
Because trout are afraid of concrete
Because dams attract too many insects
2043.e: Trout have to swim upstream to lay their eggs. Dams can block this route and harm the fish.
2043.m: Dams block the way to the spawning grounds.

2044.q: Roughly how does the number of smell cells in a dog compare with a human's?
a: A dog has many times more smell cells than a human
Dogs and humans have about the same number of smell cells
Humans have more smell cells than dogs
Dogs have no smell cells at all
2044.e: A dog is estimated to have around 220 million smell cells, a human only about 5 million. That is why a dog's nose is an important tool for exploring its surroundings.
2044.m: Dogs smell much better than people.

2045.q: Where do harbour seals usually give birth to their young?
a: Deep under water on the seabed
2045.e: Harbour seals give birth on land, often on sandbanks that dry out at low tide. The young can swim after just a few hours.
2045.m: Harbour seals are born on sandbanks.

2046.q: How can you tell the grass snake apart from the venomous adder?
a: The grass snake has round pupils
The grass snake has a zigzag stripe
The grass snake has vertical slit pupils
2046.e: Grass snakes have round pupils and half-moon patches. The adder has vertical slit pupils and a zigzag stripe.

2047.q: Where does a trout lay its eggs?
a: In a hollow in the gravel on the riverbed
In a hole in a tree
2047.e: The trout uses its tail to dig a small hollow in the gravel. It lays its eggs there so that they are protected.
2047.m: Trout eggs lie protected in the gravel.

2064.q: Why does an iceberg float in the sea instead of sinking?
a: Ice has a lower density than water
The seawater is too cold for sinking
2064.e: When water freezes, it expands and so becomes lighter per volume than liquid water. That is why ice floats on the surface of the water, even huge icebergs.
2064.m: Ice is lighter than the same amount of water.

2095.q: Which of these animals is the African wild dog most closely related to?
2095.e: Like the wolf, the African wild dog belongs to the dog family. Despite its spots, it is not closely related to hyenas.
2095.m: The wild dog is related to the wolf, not the hyena.

a: Diplomats cannot be arrested in the host country like ordinary citizens
Diplomats do not have to pay taxes in their home country
Diplomats are not allowed to vote
Diplomats have to change country every year
2097.e: Diplomatic immunity protects embassy staff from being prosecuted in the host country. This is so that they can do their work independently and safely.

2101.q: What is the difference between saving and investing?
a: Saving puts money aside safely, investing puts money in with risk to earn more
Saving and investing mean exactly the same
Saving always earns more than investing
2101.e: Saving means putting money aside safely but with little return, for example in a savings account. Investing, for example in shares, can earn more, but also carries the risk of losing money.
2101.m: Saving is safe, investing is riskier.

a: The green pigment that captures sunlight
2108.e: Chlorophyll is found in the green parts of a plant and captures sunlight for photosynthesis. It is what gives leaves their green colour.
2108.m: Chlorophyll makes leaves green and captures light.

2115.q: Which season is usually the warmest in Switzerland?
2115.e: In summer the sun is higher in the sky and the days are long. That is why it gets warmest then.

2148.q: Roughly how long do young leopards stay with their mother?
a: They leave her after a week
2148.e: The young learn to hunt from their mother. At about 18 to 24 months they become independent.
2148.m: Young leopards learn for two years.

2168.q: What by-product of photosynthesis do plants release into the air?
2168.e: In photosynthesis, plants use light energy to turn water and CO2 into glucose. Oxygen is made as a by-product and released through the stomata.
2168.m: Photosynthesis releases oxygen as a by-product.

2169.q: Who elects the government in a democracy?
2169.e: In a democracy all citizens may choose who governs them. That keeps power under control.
2169.m: The power to vote lies with the people.

2172.q: What does the Federal Department of Foreign Affairs (FDFA) do?
a: It looks after relations with other countries
2172.e: The FDFA is Switzerland’s foreign ministry. It keeps up contacts with other states and helps Swiss people abroad.
2172.m: The FDFA looks after foreign relations.

2196.q: Why is it important to get enough sleep?
a: So that your body and brain can recover
So that you get hungry faster
2196.e: While you sleep, your body recovers and your brain sorts out what you learnt during the day. Without sleep you are tired and cannot concentrate.

a: Two or more parties link their lists to work together when seats are shared out
A list of all the laws
2213.e: With a list alliance, smaller parties can add their votes together. This helps them win more seats in parliament.
2213.m: List alliances combine the votes of several parties.

2214.q: Why is a healthy breakfast important?
a: It gives you energy for the day
It makes you tired straight away
It makes you grow faster than anything else
2214.e: In the morning your body is empty and needs new energy. A good breakfast helps you learn and play.

2251.q: Which statement about the African wild dog is true?
a: It is a hunter that lives in groups
2251.e: It lives and hunts in a close-knit group. That makes it a very social predator.
2251.m: Wild dogs are very social animals.

2256.q: What is a converging lens used for, for example in glasses or a camera?
a: It brings light rays together at one point
It scatters light in all directions
It changes the colour of light
2256.e: A converging lens is thicker in the middle than at the edge and bends parallel light rays so that they meet at a focal point. This creates sharp images in cameras or on the retina.
2256.m: Converging lenses focus light at one point.

2261.q: Many African wild dogs live in the Selous Game Reserve. Which continent is it on?
2261.e: The Selous Game Reserve (now Nyerere National Park) is in the south of Tanzania in Africa. It is one of the most important areas for African wild dogs.
2261.m: The Selous Game Reserve is in Tanzania in Africa.

2272.q: Which large predator with white fur lives on the Arctic ice?
2272.e: The polar bear is the largest predator on land and lives in the Arctic, not at the South Pole. Its thick fur and a layer of fat protect it from the cold.
2272.m: The polar bear lives on the Arctic ice.

2280.q: What do two rams sometimes do to show which one is stronger?
2280.e: Rams sometimes crash their heads and horns together hard to show which one is stronger. This is called head-butting.
2280.m: Rams butt heads to test their strength.

2281.q: What is panting mainly for in dogs?
2281.e: Because dogs can hardly sweat through their bodies, they cool down by panting quickly. Moisture evaporates from the tongue and airways.

2282.q: In which habitats do you typically find the grey heron?
a: Only high in the mountains above 3000 metres
Only in thick, dark forest with no water
2282.e: The grey heron lives by all kinds of waters, as long as it can find fish and other prey there. Sometimes you can even find it by ponds in towns and cities.
2282.m: It lives where there is water.

2283.q: Why does the sparrow like living near people so much?
a: because it finds food and nesting places there
because it is afraid of trees
because it has to live in water
2283.e: In towns and villages the sparrow finds lots of crumbs and good places to nest. That is why it likes living where people live.

2284.q: What helps trout get past small obstacles such as steps in a river?
2284.e: A fish ladder is made of several small steps in the water that make it easier for fish like trout to swim upwards. This way they get past obstacles.
2284.m: Fish ladders help trout on their journeys.

2286.q: How do male sand lizards often behave towards rivals in the mating season?
a: They fight and defend their territory against other males
They always share a territory peacefully
They leave the area at once
2286.e: Rival males can really bite each other to secure their territory and access to females. Such fights are seen more often in spring.
2286.m: Males defend their territory by fighting.

2288.q: Why are hamsters often hard to hold on to when you want to catch them?
a: They can escape through small holes
2288.e: Hamsters are very quick and can slip through tiny gaps. That is why they sometimes escape from their cage very fast.

2289.q: Which well-known film character from “Madagascar” is a ring-tailed lemur?
2289.e: In the “Madagascar” films, King Julien is a ring-tailed lemur. This made the animals better known around the world.
2289.m: King Julien is a ring-tailed lemur.

2290.q: What do many aphids release from two small tubes on their back end when an enemy comes?
2290.e: The two tubes on the back end are called siphunculi. A sticky defensive substance comes out of them, which is meant to scare off enemies.
2290.m: Aphids defend themselves with a sticky substance.

2291.q: Which Swiss organisation works, among other things, to protect amphibians such as the fire salamander?
2291.e: Pro Natura works to protect endangered habitats and species in Switzerland, including amphibians such as the fire salamander. For example, it supports measures such as amphibian fences.

2292.q: Does the European pond turtle live in salt water or fresh water?
a: Only in the salt water of the sea
Only in springs high in the Alps
Neither in water nor on land
2292.e: It lives in ponds, pools and old side arms of rivers. Sea turtles, on the other hand, are a completely different group.
2292.m: Pond turtles live in fresh water.

2293.q: What do bison like doing to get rid of parasites and look after their skin?
a: They roll in dust or sand
They bathe in lakes full of fish
2293.e: The dust bath helps against annoying insects and keeps the coat in good condition. The hollows it leaves behind are called wallows.
2293.m: Dust baths keep the bison’s coat healthy.

2294.q: How does a donkey usually behave when it gets a fright?
a: It often stands still calmly instead of running away
It jumps into the air at once
2294.e: Unlike horses, which often run off at once when in danger, donkeys often stand still first and watch what is happening. This helps them react sensibly.
2294.m: Donkeys often stay calm in danger.

2295.q: What happens when a mute swan is frightened and cannot fly away?
a: it attacks with a loud hiss
it disappears under water for hours
2295.e: If the swan feels cornered, it can suddenly attack. It hisses and snorts loudly as it does so.
2295.m: In an emergency the swan attacks.

2296.q: Spiders have no bones. What protects their body?
2296.e: Spiders do not have bones inside them like we do. Instead, a hard shell protects them from the outside. This is called an exoskeleton.
2296.m: Their skeleton is on the outside of the body.

2297.q: What does a mute swan like to eat most?
2297.e: Mute swans feed mainly on plants in and around the water. Meat hardly plays a part in their diet.

2298.q: Does a starfish have a heart?
2298.e: A starfish does not have a heart like we humans do. Its body works in a completely different way.

2299.q: How does a ring-tailed lemur usually move about on the ground?
a: With long hops like a kangaroo
2299.e: On the ground the ring-tailed lemur usually walks on four legs with its tail held up. In trees it jumps and climbs skilfully.
2299.m: Ring-tailed lemurs mostly walk on four legs.

2300.q: Why are small tunnels sometimes built under roads for frogs in Switzerland?
a: So that they can travel safely to their pond
So that they can spend the winter in them
So that they can lay their eggs in them
So that they can hide from the sun
2300.e: In spring many common frogs cross roads on their way to their ponds. Tunnels and fences help them reach their goal safely without being run over.

2301.q: What does the pike use to breathe under water?
2301.e: Like all fish, the pike breathes with gills. With them it takes in the oxygen dissolved in the water.

2302.q: At about what age do young wolf pups first open their eyes?
2302.e: In their first days of life, wolf pups are blind and helpless. Only after around two weeks do they slowly open their eyes and start to explore their surroundings.
2302.m: Pups open their eyes after about two weeks.

2303.q: Why did Yugoslavia under Tito have a special role among the communist states?
a: It stayed independent of the Soviet Union and went its own way
It was the Soviet Union's most loyal ally
It was the first country to introduce capitalism
2303.e: Josip Broz Tito broke with Stalin in 1948 and led Yugoslavia as a non-aligned socialist state. The country belonged neither to NATO nor to the Warsaw Pact.
2303.m: Tito went his own socialist way.

2304.q: How does an earwig develop from egg to adult?
a: Through larval stages without a pupa
Through a pupa, like a butterfly
It hatches fully formed straight away
It grows up as a worm in water
2304.e: A larva hatches from the egg and moults several times. There is no pupal stage.
2304.m: No pupa, just larvae that moult.

2305.q: Where does the mother mole build her nest for her young?
a: In a soft chamber deep underground
2305.e: Deep in her tunnel system the mother mole builds a cosy chamber. She lines it with grass and leaves.

2306.e: Only the male roe buck has antlers on his head. They fall off every year and grow back again.

2307.q: What is an ovipositor in female dragonflies?
a: An organ for inserting eggs into plants
A tool for digging in the ground
2307.e: Many damselflies and some larger dragonflies use the ovipositor to insert eggs into plant tissue. This keeps the eggs protected.
2307.m: The ovipositor puts eggs into plants.

2309.q: Which fish family does the European perch belong to?
2309.e: The European perch, called Egli in Switzerland, belongs to the true perch family. This family also includes, for example, the zander and the ruffe.
2309.m: The perch belongs to the true perches.

2310.q: About how fast can a barn swallow fly?
2310.e: Barn swallows can reach speeds of about 50 to 60 km/h in flight. They are very agile and can change direction quickly.
2310.m: The barn swallow flies at up to 60 km/h.

2311.q: What other role do cockchafer grubs play in the ecosystem?
a: They are food for many animals
2311.e: Cockchafer grubs are food for moles, badgers, hedgehogs and birds. This makes them part of the food chain.
2311.m: Grubs are food for other animals.

2312.q: What does a squirrel often do with its tail when it is excited?
a: It flicks it quickly back and forth
It goes completely stiff for ever
2312.e: When a squirrel is excited or alarmed, its tail flicks quickly. This is how it shows its mood.
2312.m: The tail flicks when it is excited.

2313.q: Which group of animals does the harbour seal belong to, even though it has flippers?
2313.e: The harbour seal belongs to the order of carnivores, even though it looks very different from a lion or a wolf. It feeds mainly on fish.
2313.m: The harbour seal is a carnivore.

2314.q: What is the mating season like for ring-tailed lemurs?
a: It lasts only a short time each year
It happens only every ten years
2314.e: Ring-tailed lemurs mate only during a short season. Because of this, the young are born at about the same time.

2316.e: Pigs grunt to tell other pigs something. Depending on whether they are happy or afraid, the grunting sounds different.

2317.q: Why does a house fly so often escape when you try to catch it?
a: Because it spots movements very quickly
Because it smells and nobody wants to touch it
2317.e: The fly’s compound eyes detect the tiniest movement in a flash. That is why it usually flies away before a hand can catch it.
2317.m: Flies see movements in a flash.

2318.q: What are the calluses on the chest and knees of the Bactrian camel for?
a: They cushion it when it lies down on hot or hard ground
2318.e: The hard pads protect the skin when the camel lies down. That way the skin does not get injured or burnt.
2318.m: Calluses cushion and protect the skin.

2319.q: What does an earthworm do with the leaves it pulls into its tunnels?
a: It digests them into nutrient-rich humus
It builds a roof with them
2319.e: Earthworms eat leaves together with soil. What comes out is fertile humus for the soil.

2320.q: How clever are pigs thought to be compared with other domestic animals?
a: They are thought to be one of the cleverest domestic animals
They are thought to be rather unintelligent
They are less clever than fish
They cannot learn anything at all
2320.e: Studies show that pigs learn very well and can solve tasks, for example. Some researchers even compare their intelligence with that of dogs.

2321.q: Which dangerous disease must a dog be vaccinated against if it travels abroad?
2321.e: Rabies is a dangerous viral disease that can also infect humans. Switzerland is considered free of rabies, so a dog needs the vaccination mainly for trips abroad.
2321.m: Dogs need a rabies jab to travel abroad.

2322.q: Which sense is especially strong in the wolf?
2322.e: With their sensitive noses, wolves can detect tracks and prey from a long way off. Their sense of smell is much better than that of humans.
2322.m: Wolves have an excellent sense of smell.

2323.q: What kind of animal is the pike?
2323.e: The pike is a fish that hunts other animals. Fish like this are called predatory fish.
2323.m: The pike is a predatory fish.

2324.q: In which country does the okapi live in the wild?
2324.e: The okapi lives only in the rainforests in the north-east and centre of the Democratic Republic of the Congo. It is not found in the wild anywhere else.
2324.m: Okapis live only in the Congo.

2325.q: How long does a mother rhino carry her baby before it is born?
2325.e: A mother rhino carries her baby for about 15 months, which is over a year. That is much longer than in most animals.
2325.m: Rhino babies grow for 15 months before birth.

2326.q: Why do wasps have the warning colours yellow and black?
2326.e: The bright colours tell other animals: careful, I can sting. That is why many enemies prefer to leave the wasp alone.
2326.m: Yellow and black warn of a sting.

2327.q: What are the dark patches around the panda’s eyes probably for?
a: They help with camouflage and communication
2327.e: Researchers think that the dark eye patches help camouflage the panda from enemies. Other pandas can also recognise the patches.
2327.m: Eye patches camouflage and help with recognition.

2328.q: About how big does an adult hedgehog get?
2328.e: An adult hedgehog usually measures between 20 and 30 centimetres. That means it fits nicely into a flower bed or under hedges.
2328.m: Hedgehogs grow to about 20 to 30 centimetres.

2329.q: In brown bears, which sex is usually bigger and heavier?
a: Both are always the same weight
2329.e: Male brown bears are usually much bigger and heavier than the females. This difference is especially noticeable during the mating season.

2330.q: The praying mantis belongs to the group called mantises. Is it a true grasshopper?
a: No, it forms its own group of insects
Yes, it is a large bush cricket
Yes, it is a kind of cricket
2330.e: Mantises are a separate order of insects. The German name “Fangschrecke” comes from its grasping legs, but mantises are not closely related to true grasshoppers.

2331.q: Which habitat did the huge bison herds of North America mainly live in?
a: The prairie, an open grassland landscape
2331.e: The prairie offers lots of grass to eat. The herds travelled long distances there.
2331.m: Bison lived mainly on the prairie.

2332.q: What colour is a great tit’s belly?
2332.e: The great tit has a bright yellow belly. It also has a black stripe down the middle.
2332.m: Great tits have a yellow belly.

2333.q: What role does the otter play as an indicator in the ecosystem?
2333.e: Because otters can only survive in clean waters with enough fish, they are considered important indicators of healthy rivers and lakes. If they return, it is a good sign.

2334.q: How does a herd of African buffalo often defend itself against lions?
a: The animals face the attacker together
All the animals hide under the surface of the water
They bury themselves in the ground
2334.e: The herd can fight off attackers with their horns. Sometimes buffalo even rescue a herd member in danger.
2334.m: Together, buffalo are strong against attackers.

2335.q: How many cubs does a female brown bear usually have in one litter?
2335.e: A female brown bear usually has one to three cubs, sometimes four. The cubs are born during the winter rest in the safety of the den.
2335.m: Brown bears usually have two cubs.

2336.q: Whose droppings do minotaur beetles and their larvae often feed on?
2336.e: The minotaur beetle carries rabbit or sheep droppings into its tunnels. There they serve as a food store for the larvae.
2336.m: Minotaur beetles collect rabbit and sheep droppings.

2337.q: Does the sparrow fly to a warm country in winter?
a: no, it stays here all year
yes, it always flies to Africa
yes, it flies to the North Pole
yes, it flies to an island
2337.e: Sparrows are resident birds, which means they stay in one place all year round. So they have to find food here in winter too.
2337.m: Sparrows don’t fly away in winter.

2338.q: Which animal are all pet rabbits descended from?
2338.e: All pet rabbits were bred from the European wild rabbit many hundreds of years ago. That is why they still look similar.
2338.m: Pet rabbits come from the wild rabbit.

2339.q: How do budgies often greet each other with their beaks?
a: They pull each other’s feathers out
2339.e: Budgies often greet each other by gently touching beaks. It is a friendly gesture between friends.
2339.m: A gentle beak touch is a greeting.

2341.q: What is typical of the shape of the great crested grebe’s beak?
a: It is pointed and dagger-like, good for catching fish
It is broad and flat like a duck’s
It is strongly hooked like a bird of prey’s
It is tiny and hardly visible
2341.e: The pointed, dagger-like beak is excellent for catching slippery fish under water. It is also used as a signal during courtship.
2341.m: The beak is as pointed as a dagger.

2342.q: Does the mother slow worm look after her young?
a: No, the young are independent from the start
Yes, she feeds them in the nest
Yes, she carries them on her back
2342.e: The young have to manage on their own straight after birth. They soon eat small prey.
2342.m: Young slow worms are independent at once.

2343.q: About how much does an adult barn owl weigh?
2343.e: An adult barn owl weighs about as much as three bars of chocolate, so around 300 to 350 grams. That is why it flies so lightly.
2343.m: It weighs only a few hundred grams.

a: No, they have a horny beak
Only a few teeth at the front
2344.e: Sea turtles have no teeth. Instead they have a hard beak made of horn, which they use to break up their food.
2344.m: Instead of teeth they have a horny beak.

2345.q: Does rhino horn really help against illnesses, as some people believe?
a: No, that has not been proven
2345.e: Scientists have shown that the horn has no special healing power. It is made only of keratin, like our fingernails. Sadly, rhinos are still hunted for it.
2345.m: The horn has no healing power.

2346.q: When are chamois kids usually born?
2346.e: Most chamois kids are born in late spring, in May or June. By then there is already enough fresh green food in the mountains for the mother.
2346.m: Chamois kids are born in May or June.

2347.q: How does a pig use its snout to explore its surroundings?
a: It feels and smells things very precisely with it
It sees in the dark with it
It drinks with it like a straw
2347.e: The snout is full of sensitive nerves. With it, the pig feels and smells everything very precisely.
2347.m: The snout is for both touch and smell.

2348.q: What happens to a sick or very old bee in the hive?
a: Other bees carry it out of the hive
2348.e: Everything in the hive must stay clean so that diseases do not spread. That is why healthy bees carry dead or sick bees out of the hive.
2348.m: Sick bees are carried out of the hive.

2349.e: The octopus lives in salty sea water, often near the coast or in the deep sea. It is not found in fresh water.
2349.m: The octopus lives in the sea.

2350.q: What does the brown trout use to take in oxygen from the water?
2350.e: Water flows through the mouth and over the gills. There the oxygen passes into the blood.

2352.q: Which is usually bigger, the male or the female garden spider?
a: Both are always exactly the same size
2352.e: Female garden spiders are much bigger than the males. They need the bigger body to carry lots of eggs.

2353.q: What are some kinds of duck, such as the tufted duck, especially good at?
2353.e: Diving ducks such as the tufted duck go right under water to look for food on the bottom. Dabbling ducks, on the other hand, do not dive as deep.

2354.q: What does the Roman snail use to move?
2354.e: The snail glides on a single broad muscular foot. It moves in wave-like motions.

2355.q: How should you approach a guinea pig before you pick it up?
2355.e: Guinea pigs are easily frightened. That is why it is important to approach them slowly and calmly so that they feel safe.
2355.m: Always approach a guinea pig calmly and carefully.

2356.q: Which sense is especially good in the rhino?
2356.e: A rhino has a very good sense of smell and can recognise enemies or friends from far away. Its sense of smell is more important than its eyes.
2356.m: Rhinos have an excellent sense of smell.

2357.q: About how many aphids can a ladybird eat in a single day?
2357.e: Ladybirds are very greedy and can eat several dozen aphids in a day. That is why they are a great help to gardeners.
2357.m: A ladybird eats lots of aphids a day.

2358.q: What is the male roe deer called?
2358.e: The male roe deer is called a roe buck. Only he has antlers.

2359.q: What do pet rabbits absolutely need when they are kept?
a: Enough space to hop and hide
A small cage with no run
2359.e: Rabbits need lots of space to hop and hide. Other rabbits and a run are also important for their wellbeing.

2360.q: Which animal is often called the “king of the animals”?
2360.e: The lion lives in Africa in groups called prides. Because of its mane and strength it is often called the king of the animals.
2360.m: The lion is the king of the savannah.

2361.q: On average, how many hours a day does a cat sleep?
2361.e: Cats are champion sleepers and often doze for 12 to 16 hours a day. This saves energy for hunting.
2361.m: Cats sleep for half the day.

2362.q: What colour is an adult peregrine falcon’s back usually?
