It only shows they are bored
They do it out of fear
3749.e: When playing, young otters train, for example, their agility and skill in the water. This prepares them for hunting later on.

3750.q: What is a female cow that has not yet had a calf called?
3750.e: A young female cow that has not yet given birth to a calf is called a heifer. Only after her first calf is she called a cow.
3750.m: Young female cattle are called heifers.

3751.q: Why is a koala quite fussy about what it eats?
a: It only likes certain kinds of eucalyptus
It only eats leaves from the ground
3751.e: Of the many kinds of eucalyptus, the koala only likes very particular ones. It chooses them carefully with its fine nose.
3751.m: Koalas only like certain kinds of eucalyptus.

3752.q: What is a baby roe deer called?
3752.e: A little roe deer is called a fawn. It has a spotted coat.
3752.m: A baby roe deer is called a fawn.

3753.q: How does a housefly best find its food?
a: It smells it from far away with its antennae
3753.e: With its fine antennae the housefly can pick up smells from some distance away. This way it quickly finds something to eat.

3754.q: How does the weasel usually live socially?
3754.e: Weasels defend their hunting territory against other weasels and meet mainly in the mating season. Outside that time they live alone.

3755.q: How old does a wood mouse usually get in the wild?
3755.e: In the wild, wood mice usually only live for about a year because they have many enemies.
3755.m: Often only about one year old.

3756.q: About how long is a giraffe's tongue?
a: About as long as a finger
3756.e: The giraffe's tongue is very long and flexible. With it, it can reach for leaves even between the thorns of the acacia.
3756.m: Giraffe tongues are about 45 centimetres long.

3757.q: How many calves does a female African buffalo usually have at once?
3757.e: Usually only one calf is born. It can soon follow the herd.
3757.m: Usually only one calf is born.

3758.q: What job do the antennae of a pond skater have?
a: They sense signals from the surroundings
3758.e: With its antennae the animal senses touch and smells. This helps it find its way on the water.

3759.q: How do cockerels usually look different from hens?
a: Cockerels are bigger and more colourful
3759.e: Male chickens, cockerels, are often bigger than hens and have a more striking, colourful set of feathers. You can usually recognise them at first glance.
3759.m: Cockerels are bigger and more colourful.

3760.e: It pushes itself forward with sideways bends of its body. It has no legs.

3761.q: What is the name of the hilly area in the canton of Solothurn with many small villages?
3761.e: The Bucheggberg is a rural area in the canton of Solothurn with fields, forests and small villages. The Emmental and the Seeland are in the canton of Bern, the Toggenburg in St Gallen.
3761.m: The Bucheggberg is a rural region in the canton of Solothurn.

3762.q: What does a jackal's tail look like?
3762.e: The tail is covered in bushy fur. It helps jackals communicate with each other.

3763.q: Why can stag beetle larvae survive in wood for so long?
a: The rotten wood is their food and their hiding place
They sleep in water every night
3763.e: In the ground they are protected and always find food. They grow slowly because their food is low in nutrients.
3763.m: Wood is food and hiding place at once.

3764.q: Which way of walking do camels use, moving both legs on one side of the body at the same time?
3764.e: Camels pace, which means they move both legs on one side together. This gives them their typical rocking walk.
3764.m: Camels walk with a pacing gait.

3765.q: What are the especially long, pointed teeth of a lion called?
3765.e: The long, pointed teeth in a lion's mouth are called canines. The lion uses them to bite firmly into its prey.
3765.m: Canines are the long lion teeth.

3766.q: What do you measure when you take someone's blood pressure?
a: How strongly the blood pushes against the walls of the vessels
How much oxygen is in the blood
3766.e: Blood pressure shows how strongly the blood pushes against the walls of the arteries. It is given as two numbers, for example 120 over 80.
3766.m: Blood pressure is the pressure of the blood in the vessels.

3767.q: About how far can a chamois jump in one leap?
3767.e: As well as jumping high, chamois can also make long leaps of up to six metres. This helps them get across gorges or cracks in the rock.
3767.m: Chamois can jump up to six metres.

3768.q: How does a great tit defend its territory against other great tits?
a: It doesn't, it always shares everything
3768.e: Male great tits sing loudly to mark their territory. When there are intruders, they also make threatening gestures such as raising their feathers.
3768.m: Song protects the great tit's territory.

3769.q: How do ibex usually live outside the mating season?
a: Males and females form separate herds
All the animals live together in one herd all year
Each animal lives completely on its own
They live in pairs like birds
3769.e: Outside the mating season the males usually stay in all-male herds, while the females form their own groups with their young. Only in the rutting season in winter do the two groups meet.
3769.m: Males and females usually live apart.

3770.q: Which people kept alpacas many hundreds of years ago?
3770.e: In the Andes, the Inca and earlier peoples already kept alpacas for their wool. The animal was very valuable to them.

3771.q: Which body position does a gorilla only rarely hold for long?
3771.e: Gorillas can stand upright for a short time, for example when beating their chest. But most of the time they move on all fours.

3772.q: How many hearts does an earthworm have?
3772.e: An earthworm does not have just one heart like us, but five pairs of small hearts. They pump the blood through its long body.

3774.q: What do ants do when part of their nest is destroyed?
a: They all fly away at once
3774.e: Ants work together as a team. If their nest is damaged, many workers repair it together.

3775.q: When is the mating season for Bactrian camels?
3775.e: The rut takes place in winter. The males are especially excitable then.

a: Areas of the Earth with a similar, typical climate
Areas at the same height above sea level
3776.e: The Earth is roughly divided into tropical, temperate and polar climate zones. They differ mainly in temperature and precipitation.
3776.m: Climate zones show the typical weather conditions of a region.

3777.q: Which animal has a hard shell and moves very slowly?
3777.e: The tortoise always carries its shell with it for protection. Some species can live for more than a hundred years.
3777.m: The tortoise carries its house with it.

3778.q: Which small invertebrates are also part of the red kite's diet?
3778.e: As well as small mammals and carrion, the red kite also eats earthworms, which it finds, for example, on freshly ploughed fields. This shows how varied its diet is.
3778.m: Earthworms are on the menu too.

3780.q: About how old can wild carrion crows get?
3780.e: In the wild, carrion crows usually reach an age of about 10 to 15 years. In human care they can live much longer.
3780.m: Carrion crows often live over ten years.

3781.q: Apart from its nose, what else does a hippo close when it dives?
3781.e: When diving, the hippo also folds its ears tightly shut so that no water gets in. Its body is well made for diving.

3782.q: Where does the water louse live?
a: Under tree bark in the forest
In the sea on coral reefs
3782.e: The water louse lives in still and slow-flowing water. It feeds on leaves and plant remains.
3782.m: The water louse lives in fresh water.

3783.q: Is the great spotted woodpecker a migratory bird?
a: No, it usually stays here all year
Yes, it flies to Africa in winter
Yes, it flies to America every winter
No, it only flies away in summer
3783.e: The great spotted woodpecker usually stays in its territory all year. So it does not have to make a long journey.

3784.q: What is it called when dolphins swim along in the waves in front of boats?
3784.e: Dolphins like to swim right in front of boats in the bow wave. This is called bow riding and they clearly enjoy it.
3784.m: Dolphins like riding the bow wave.

3785.q: What helps the giraffe eat thorny acacia branches?
3785.e: Thick, sticky saliva coats the thorns when swallowing so that they do not hurt the giraffe's throat. Its flexible lips also help it pick the leaves skilfully.

3786.q: How are young slow worms born?
a: Alive, the eggs develop inside the mother
They split off from the mother
3786.e: In slow worms the eggs stay inside the mother's body. The young hatch from the thin egg membrane shortly before or during birth.
3786.m: Slow worms give birth to live young.

3787.q: How many eggs does a female raven usually lay in a clutch?
3787.e: A raven's clutch usually has three to six eggs. The exact number depends, among other things, on how much food there is.

3789.q: What is the whole change from egg to maggot and pupa to fly called?
3789.e: This process is called complete metamorphosis. Many insects go through these four stages.

3790.q: What happens to things a kingfisher cannot digest, such as fish bones, in its stomach?
a: It coughs them up again as a pellet
It only gets rid of them as droppings
It collects them as material for its nest
3790.e: The kingfisher cannot digest fish bones and scales and coughs them up again as small pellets. Owls do this too.
3790.m: Fish bones are coughed up as pellets.

3791.q: How can you often recognise a male European pond turtle?
a: The lower shell curves slightly inwards
The shell is much bigger than the female's
It always has a red shell
3791.e: The curve helps the males when mating. Males also have a longer, thicker tail.
3791.m: Males have an inward-curving lower shell.

3792.q: What colour is the tip of the tail of many African wild dogs?
3792.e: The white tail tip works like a signal. It helps the animals keep each other in sight when hunting in tall grass.
3792.m: The white tail tip helps them find their way.

3794.q: About how tall can an adult chimpanzee get?
a: About as tall as a person
3794.e: An adult chimpanzee grows to about one to one and a half metres tall. That makes it roughly as tall as a smaller person.
3794.m: Chimpanzees are about the size of a person.

3795.q: What is it called when a cockerel calls out its loud “cock-a-doodle-doo”?
3795.e: The cockerel's typical call is called crowing. It is much louder than the quiet clucking of the hens.
3795.m: A cockerel crows rather than chirps.

3796.q: How well can a wood mouse smell and hear?
a: Very well, which helps it look for food
It cannot smell anything at all
It smells less well than a person
3796.e: The wood mouse has a very good sense of smell and hearing. This means it finds food even in the dark and notices danger in time.
3796.m: A good sense of smell and good hearing.

3797.q: Can beech martens pull in their claws like a cat?
a: No, the claws are always visible
3797.e: Unlike cats, beech martens cannot pull in their claws. The claws help them climb and dig.
3797.m: A beech marten's claws always stay out.

3798.q: The scientific name of the swift means “without feet”. Why does it fit?
a: Because it hardly uses its short feet
Because it has no legs at all
Because it hides its feet in the water
3798.e: The name Apus comes from Greek and means “without feet”. The swift does have feet, but it almost never lands and only needs them for clinging on.

3800.q: At best, how old can a wild kestrel get?
3800.e: Most kestrels in the wild only live a few years, but some individuals can reach over 10 years. Many young birds do not survive their first year.

3801.q: Which horse breed originally comes from Switzerland?
3801.e: The Freiberger is the best-known horse breed in Switzerland. It originally comes from the Jura.
3801.m: The Freiberger is a Swiss horse.

3802.q: What does the shell of the European pond turtle typically look like?
a: Dark brown to black with yellow dots or lines
3802.e: The dark colour with the yellow pattern helps it stay camouflaged in the water. The pattern is a little different on every animal.
3802.m: A dark shell with yellow dots.

3803.q: What sometimes happens during the day when small birds discover a resting tawny owl?
a: They swarm around it and scold it loudly; this is called mobbing
They all fly away at once
3803.e: Small birds such as tits or blackbirds often recognise the tawny owl as an enemy and circle it noisily to drive it away. This behaviour is called mobbing and helps birdwatchers find tawny owls.
3803.m: Small birds mob resting tawny owls.

a: Supplying West Berlin by aeroplane during a Soviet blockade
A bridge that linked East and West Berlin
3804.e: When the Soviet Union blocked the land routes to West Berlin, the Western powers supplied the city from the air for almost a year. This meant West Berlin could be held.
3804.m: The Airlift supplied West Berlin from the air.

3805.q: What were great crested grebes hunted heavily for in the 19th century?
a: For their feathers, which were put on hats
For their meat as a delicacy
3805.e: At that time the silky feathers were used by the fashion industry to decorate hats. This led to a sharp fall in many populations.
3805.m: Feather fashion put the great crested grebe in danger.

3806.q: How good is a golden eagle's eyesight compared with a person's?
a: Several times better than a person's
About as good as a person's
The golden eagle can hardly see anything
3806.e: Golden eagles have excellent eyesight and can spot prey from a great distance. Their eyes are many times sharper than human eyes.
3806.m: Golden eagles see much more sharply than people.

a: Never in the middle of the night
3807.e: Kangaroos are most active at dawn and dusk, so early in the morning and in the evening. During the day they often rest in the shade.
3807.m: Kangaroos are active in the morning and evening.

3808.q: In which country is Kruger National Park, where wild dogs live?
3808.e: Wild dogs live in Kruger National Park in South Africa. It is one of the best-known protected areas in Africa.
3808.m: Wild dogs live in Kruger National Park.

3809.q: Why did the beaver disappear from Switzerland in the 19th century?
a: A disease killed all the beavers
3809.e: People hunted the beaver for its fur, its meat and a scented substance that was used as medicine. That is why it disappeared completely from Switzerland.
3809.m: Hunting once wiped out the beaver.

3810.q: How often does a female adder usually have young?
3810.e: Carrying young takes a lot of energy. That is why many females take a year off.
3810.m: Females need time to recover between litters.

3811.q: What do young birds in the nest do when there is little food in bad weather?
a: They lower their body temperature to save energy
They leave the nest at once
They eat plants instead of insects
They call loudly for their parents all day
3811.e: When food is short, young swifts can fall into a kind of cold stiffness. This way they use less energy and get through bad days.
3811.m: Young birds save energy when hungry.

3812.q: Which feature makes fire salamanders different from lizards?
a: Fire salamanders have moist skin without scales
Fire salamanders have scales like lizards
Fire salamanders have a snail shell
3812.e: Unlike lizards, which have dry, scaly skin, the fire salamander's skin is smooth and moist. This helps it breathe through its skin.
3812.m: Its skin is moist instead of scaly.

3813.q: How many toes does a wild boar have on each foot?
3813.e: Wild boar have four toes on each foot. They leave typical tracks in soft ground.
3813.m: A wild boar has four toes per foot.

3816.q: What is typical of the bearded vulture's call?
a: It is rather quiet and rarely heard
It caws extremely loudly like a crow
3816.e: Unlike many other birds, the bearded vulture is quite silent and only calls rarely. That is why you usually recognise it by its looks and not by its sound.

3818.q: Which kind of duck is especially common in Switzerland?
3818.e: The mallard is the most common wild duck in Switzerland. You find it at almost every lake and river.
3818.m: The mallard is the most common duck.

3819.q: Which animal has a very good memory and a long trunk?
3819.e: The elephant is the largest land animal on Earth and is considered very clever. With its trunk it can grab, drink and smell.
3819.m: The elephant has a trunk and a good memory.

3820.q: In which season do you most often hear the loud chorus of tree frogs?
a: In spring, during the mating season
3820.e: During the mating season in spring, many males call at the same time at ponds. This loud chorus is typical of this season.
3820.m: The tree frog chorus rings out in spring.

3821.q: What should you think about before getting a goldfish as a pet?
a: Whether you have enough space, time and knowledge to look after it
Whether you can give it a name like a dog
3821.e: Before keeping goldfish, you should know how much space and care they need. A tank that is too small makes the animals ill.

3822.q: How does a centipede often move compared with a millipede?
a: Not at all, it stays stuck
3822.e: As hunters, centipedes have to catch their prey. Many species, such as the stone centipede, run very quickly.

3824.q: How endangered is the African elephant today, according to conservationists?
a: It is not endangered at all
There are far too many of them
3824.e: Because of poaching and the loss of its habitat, the African elephant is considered an endangered species. Conservation organisations therefore work to protect it.
3824.m: The elephant is considered endangered today.

3825.q: What colour is cows' hair usually?
a: There are many colours such as brown, black or white
3825.e: Cows can have very different coat colours depending on the breed. Some are one colour, others are spotted.
3825.m: Cow coats come in many different colours.

3826.q: How many eggs does a female sparrow usually lay at once?
3826.e: A female sparrow usually lays four to six small eggs in her nest. After about two weeks the chicks hatch from them.
3826.m: A sparrow lays about five eggs.

3827.e: UNESCO is a UN organisation that protects schools, research and important cultural sites. For example, it draws up the World Heritage List.
3827.m: UNESCO protects education, science and culture.

3828.q: About how often should you change the water in a goldfish tank?
a: Regularly, for example part of it every week
Only when the fish is ill
3828.e: To keep the water clean, you should regularly change part of it. This stops harmful substances staying in the water for too long.
3828.m: Changing the water regularly keeps fish healthy.

3829.q: How long do kingfisher parents sit on their eggs?
3829.e: The incubation lasts about 19 to 21 days. The male and female take turns sitting on the eggs.

3830.q: How does the mallard behave in towns compared with other wild ducks?
a: It adapts very well to life in towns
It dies straight away near people
3830.e: The mallard copes better with people and towns than many other wild ducks. That is why you see it so often in parks and on town ponds.

3831.q: Which three parts is the body of an earwig divided into?
3831.e: Like all insects, the earwig is made up of head, thorax and abdomen. The legs and wings are attached to the thorax.
3831.m: An insect's body consists of head, thorax and abdomen.

3833.q: Can a mole also walk backwards through its tunnels?
a: Yes, it is very good at it
No, it cannot do that at all
Only with help from other animals
3833.e: Thanks to its smooth fur and its sensitive tail, the mole can easily walk backwards through narrow tunnels. This is handy when it cannot turn round.
3833.m: Moles are good at walking backwards.

3835.q: Why do some polar bears move further north in summer?
a: To stay near the ice and find seals
To lie in the warmth there
3835.e: In summer the ice melts first in areas further south. That is why some polar bears move north, where there is still ice.
3835.m: Polar bears follow the ice north.

3836.q: What do common toad tadpoles often do in the water?
a: They swim in large dark swarms
3836.e: Common toad tadpoles often stay together in large groups and swim as a dark swarm. This also makes them a bit safer from enemies.
3836.m: Tadpoles like to swim in swarms.

3837.q: What happens to the body temperature of the edible dormouse during hibernation?
a: It changes a lot every minute
3837.e: During hibernation the edible dormouse's body temperature drops almost to the temperature around it. This saves a huge amount of energy.
3837.m: Body temperature drops sharply in hibernation.

3838.q: Roughly how big is the territory of a pair of bearded vultures?
3838.e: A pair of bearded vultures needs a very large area in the mountains as its habitat. There they look for enough food for themselves and their young.

3839.q: How do budgies in a flock communicate with each other?
3839.e: Budgies call and chirp a lot to stay in contact with each other. This keeps the flock together.

3840.q: Which animal is known for being slow and carries its shell on its back like a house?
3840.e: The tortoise always carries its hard shell with it like a house. When in danger, it can hide its head and legs completely inside.
3840.m: The tortoise carries its house with it.

3841.q: Which subspecies of brown bear is known for being especially large and lives on an island in Alaska?
3841.e: The Kodiak bear lives on the Kodiak Islands off Alaska and is one of the largest land predators in the world. It is a subspecies of the brown bear.
3841.m: The Kodiak bear is the largest brown bear.

3842.q: How does the garden spider catch its prey?
a: It wraps it in silk threads
It immediately gives it a deadly bite
It eats it whole straight away
3842.e: When an insect gets caught in the web, the spider runs over and wraps it in threads. Then it can no longer escape.
3842.m: It wraps its prey up tightly.

3843.q: What is the rearmost section of an insect's body called?
3843.e: Insect bodies have three parts: head, thorax and abdomen. You can see this well in the stag beetle.
3843.m: Insects have a head, thorax and abdomen.

3844.q: How do meerkats behave towards other groups in their territory?
a: They defend their territory, sometimes by fighting
3844.e: Meerkats defend their area against other groups. This can lead to fierce clashes.

3845.q: What does the pond skater mainly use its back legs for?
3845.e: The back legs steer the pond skater like a rudder. This lets it change direction.
3845.m: Back legs steer like a rudder.

3846.q: At what time of day is the common wall lizard mainly active?
a: During the day, especially when the sun shines
Round the clock without a break
3846.e: As a cold-blooded animal, the wall lizard needs the warmth of the sun to become active. That is why it is active during the day.

3847.q: How many earthworms can live in good meadow soil in a patch as big as a bath towel?
3847.e: Very many earthworms live in good meadow soil. In such a small patch there can be over a hundred, sometimes even several hundred.
3847.m: Many worms live in good soil.

3848.q: What sound does a wild boar often make?
3848.e: Wild boar often communicate with grunting sounds. This way they stay in contact within the group.

3849.q: What are the feet of the great tit, which it uses to hold on to branches, like?
3849.e: The great tit has feet with four toes, three pointing forwards and one backwards. With them it can hold on to branches very well.
3849.m: Four toes help it hold on to branches.

3850.q: How does a gorilla mother carry her little baby at first?
a: In a nest in the water
3850.e: In the first months the baby gorilla clings to its mother's belly. Later it climbs onto her back.

3851.q: What is the okapi often also called because of its appearance?
3851.e: The name forest giraffe fits because the okapi lives in the forest and is related to the giraffe. But it is not a zebra.
3851.m: The okapi is also called the forest giraffe.

3852.q: How often do wolves really attack people?
a: Very rarely, wolves usually avoid people
Almost every day in every forest
Always, as soon as they see a person
Only at night, but then very often
3852.e: Wolves are naturally rather shy and avoid contact with people. Attacks on people are extremely rare and hardly ever happen.
3852.m: Wolves only very rarely attack people.

3853.q: What can one toe on a barn owl's foot do that is special?
a: It can point forwards or backwards
It has no claw at all
It is twice as long as the others
3853.e: The barn owl has a reversible toe that can be turned forwards or backwards. This lets it grip and hold prey especially well.
3853.m: A movable toe helps with gripping.

3854.q: How do mute swan parents behave towards their cygnets in the first weeks?
a: They protect them and lead them everywhere
They leave them alone in the nest
They take them to other birds
3854.e: The parents stay very close to their cygnets and lead them to good feeding places. This way the young quickly learn how to survive.
3854.m: Parents go everywhere with their cygnets.

3855.q: What do llamas have at the top front of their mouth instead of incisors?
a: Nothing, just gums with no purpose
3855.e: Like cattle, llamas have a hard pad at the top front. They press grass against it with their lower incisors and pull it off.
3855.m: Llamas have a dental pad at the top front.

3856.q: What do the humps of a Bactrian camel mainly store?
3856.e: The humps contain fatty tissue that serves as an energy reserve. Water is not stored in the hump.

3857.q: How good is a brown bear's sense of smell?
a: Very good, much better than a person's
Brown bears cannot smell at all
Only as good as a fish's
3857.e: Brown bears have an excellent sense of smell and can scent food over long distances. This sense is their most important tool when looking for food.
3857.m: Brown bears have a particularly good sense of smell.

3858.q: Which habitat does the European pond turtle like best?
a: Still or slow-flowing water with a muddy bottom
3858.e: There it finds food and hiding places in the mud. Sunny spots on the bank are also important.
3858.m: Calm water with mud is ideal.

3859.q: What does it mean when a proposal in a vote is ‘thrown out’?
3859.e: If more people say No than Yes, a proposal is thrown out, that is, rejected. Then everything stays as it was.

3860.q: What colour is a grasshopper often?
3860.e: The colours help it hide in the grass. This makes it harder for enemies to see it.
3860.m: Its colour camouflages it in the grass.

3862.q: How does a red fox usually behave towards people in the wild?
a: It is usually very shy and careful
It always runs straight towards people
It attacks people all the time
It begs to be stroked like a dog
3862.e: In the wild the red fox is usually very shy and prefers to keep out of people's way. In towns, though, some foxes have become bolder.

3863.q: What role does an experienced lead nanny goat often have in the herd?
a: She leads the herd and the others follow her
She is always the only one asleep
She never eats with the others
3863.e: An experienced, often older female goat frequently leads the herd. The other goats follow her lead, for example when it comes to which way to go.
3863.m: The lead goat leads the herd.

3864.q: What does a trout live on in the first days after hatching?
a: A small yolk sac on its belly
3864.e: Newly hatched trout carry a small sac of food on their belly. They live off it until they can feed themselves.
3864.m: Young trout have a yolk sac on their belly.

3865.q: What does a male common wall lizard often do to defend its territory?
a: It shows itself off and drives rivals away
It leaves its territory at once
It sings loudly like a bird
3865.e: Males show their strength by nodding their heads and behaving in a showy way. This drives other males out of their territory.
3865.m: Territories are defended in a showy way.

3866.q: Where does the name “ladybird” probably come from?
a: From the Virgin Mary, “Our Lady”, in the Christian religion
From a girl called Lady who discovered the beetle
3866.e: In the past people believed the helpful little beetle was a gift from the Virgin Mary to farmers. That is probably where its name comes from.
3866.m: The name recalls the Virgin Mary.
